o: Muslim divorced women cannot approach Section 125 at all
Section 125 applies only to Hindu women
Maintenance ends automatically after iddat in all cases
A Muslim divorced woman can seek maintenance under Section 125 CrPC even after the iddat period, until she remarries
questions.e: Shabana Bano (2010) held that Section 125 is a social-justice provision available to divorced Muslim women beyond the iddat period until remarriage, reconciling it with the 1986 Act as interpreted in Danial Latifi.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act, 1956 governs Hindu adoptions. Section 11 requires, inter alia, that if the adopter is male and the child female (or vice versa), the age gap must be at least 21 years. A 30-year-old man seeks to adopt a 10-year-old girl. Under the stated principle:
o: The adoption is valid without conditions
Age gaps apply only to sons
The adoption violates Section 11's 21-year age-gap requirement for opposite-sex adoptions and cannot proceed
Adoption under HAMA needs no age conditions
questions.e: Section 11(vi) HAMA mandates a minimum 21-year age difference where the adopter and adoptee are of opposite sexes; a 20-year gap fails the requirement, rendering the adoption impermissible.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Under Section 14 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, property possessed by a female Hindu becomes her absolute property. In Vineeta Sharma (2020), the Supreme Court affirmed daughters' coparcenary rights by birth. A daughter claims partition of ancestral property; her brothers argue she married before 2005. Under the stated principle:
o: Married daughters are excluded from coparcenary rights
Marital status is irrelevant; a daughter is a coparcener by birth under the amended Section 6
The claim fails because the father died before 2005
questions.e: Vineeta Sharma (2020) held daughters are coparceners by birth under Section 6 as amended in 2005, irrespective of marital status or the father's survival on the amendment date.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 defines 'domestic relationship' in Section 2(f) to include relationships in the nature of marriage. In D. Velusamy v. D. Patchaiammal (2010), the Supreme Court laid down criteria for such relationships. A woman in a long-term shared-household relationship alleging violence seeks a residence order. Under the stated principle:
o: She has no remedy because they were not married
The DV Act applies only to married women
She may claim protection if the relationship satisfies the Velusamy criteria of a relationship in the nature of marriage — shared household, long duration, holding out as spouses
Residence orders are available only against husbands
questions.e: The DV Act expressly covers relationships in the nature of marriage; D. Velusamy (2010) gave criteria (age of majority, qualification to marry, significant cohabitation, shared household) for identifying them.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 provides a secular form of marriage. Section 5 requires 30 days' notice of intended marriage, during which objections under Section 7 may be raised. An inter-faith couple seeks to marry under the Act. Under the stated principle:
o: They must convert to one religion first
They can marry under the Special Marriage Act after the 30-day notice procedure, without conversion
The Act applies only to Hindus
Notice is required only for foreign nationals
questions.e: The Special Marriage Act, 1954 enables civil marriage irrespective of religion; Section 5's 30-day notice and Section 7's objection procedure are the statutory safeguards, with no conversion requirement.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: In Githa Hariharan v. Reserve Bank of India (1999), the Supreme Court interpreted Section 6(a) of the Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956 — which named the father as natural guardian 'and after him' the mother. The Court held that:
o: Mothers can never be natural guardians
The provision was struck down entirely
'After him' means in the father's absence, so the mother can act as natural guardian when the father is unavailable or indifferent
questions.e: Githa Hariharan (1999) read 'after him' in Section 6(a) to mean 'in the absence of' the father, enabling mothers to act as natural guardians where the father is absent, indifferent or unable, advancing gender equality.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The 1st Amendment (1951) added Articles 31A and 31B with the Ninth Schedule, and inserted clause (4) in Article 15. Its immediate provocation was:
o: The Supreme Court's decision in Champakam Dorairajan (1951) striking down caste-based reservations and the Patna High Court's decision in Kameshwar Singh striking down the Bihar Land Reforms Act
questions.e: Champakam Dorairajan (Supreme Court, 1951) struck down the Communal G.O. reserving seats by community, and Kameshwar Singh (Patna High Court, 1951) struck down the Bihar Land Reforms Act, 1950. Parliament responded with the 1st Amendment: Articles 31A and 31B, the Ninth Schedule, and Article 15(4) enabling special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The 24th Amendment (1971) was Parliament's response to Golaknath (1967). It:
o: Declared that Parliament may amend any part of the Constitution including fundamental rights, and made the President's assent to amendment Bills obligatory
questions.e: The 24th Amendment (1971) amended Articles 13 and 368 to assert Parliament's power to amend fundamental rights and to require the President to assent to Constitution Amendment Bills, directly countering Golaknath.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The 26th Amendment (1971) is known for:
o: Abolishing the privy purses and privileges of former rulers of princely states
questions.e: The 26th Amendment (1971) derecognised former rulers and abolished their privy purses, after the Supreme Court had struck down the earlier executive order in Madhav Rao Scindia (1970).

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The 91st Amendment (2003) is associated with:
o: Capping the size of the Council of Ministers at 15% of the legislative house's strength and barring defectors from ministerial office until re-election
questions.e: The 91st Amendment (2003) limited ministries to 15% of the House's membership and disqualified defectors under the Tenth Schedule from holding ministerial or remunerative political posts until re-elected.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The 99th Amendment (2014), which inserted Articles 124A–124C for the National Judicial Appointments Commission, was:
o: Struck down 4:1 in Supreme Court Advocates-on-Record Association v. Union of India (2015) for violating judicial independence, a basic feature
questions.e: The Fourth Judges case (2015) struck down the 99th Amendment and the NJAC Act 4:1, holding that the primacy of the judiciary in appointments is part of the basic structure, reviving the collegium system.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The 106th Amendment (2023), the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, provides:
o: Immediate 50% reservation for women in all legislatures
33% reservation for women in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies, effective after delimitation following the next census
Reservation for women in the Rajya Sabha
Reservation for women in local bodies only
questions.e: The 106th Amendment (2023) reserves one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies, but its commencement is tied to delimitation after the census following the amendment.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Delegated legislation is valid only within the limits of the parent statute; excessive delegation of essential legislative functions is unconstitutional. In Re Delhi Laws Act (1951), the Supreme Court held Parliament cannot delegate its essential legislative function. A statute authorises the executive to 'modify any provision of the Act as it deems fit, including its policy.' Under the stated principle:
o: The delegation is valid because Parliament is supreme
Delegated legislation can never be challenged
The delegation is excessive and unconstitutional because laying down legislative policy is an essential legislative function that cannot be delegated
questions.e: Re Delhi Laws Act (1951) prohibits delegation of essential legislative functions, including the determination of legislative policy; a Henry VIII clause letting the executive rewrite the Act's policy is excessive delegation.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Promissory estoppel prevents the government from resiling from a promise where a citizen has altered his position relying on it, as in Motilal Padampat Sugar Mills v. State of U.P. (1979). A State announces a tax exemption to attract industry; a company invests crores relying on it; the State withdraws the exemption prematurely. Under the stated principle:
o: The State can withdraw freely because policy changes are sovereign
The company can invoke promissory estoppel because it altered its position on the faith of the government's promise
Estoppel never applies against the government
The company must prove a written contract
questions.e: Motilal Padampat (1979) held the government bound by promissory estoppel where a promise intended to be acted upon induces detrimental reliance; the State can resile only on overriding public interest with due process.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Judicial review of administrative action in India examines decision-making on grounds of illegality, irrationality and procedural impropriety. The Wednesbury principle (Associated Provincial Picture Houses v. Wednesbury, 1948) tests unreasonableness. An authority bans all street vendors in a city without any study, hearing or rationale. Under the stated principle, the decision is vulnerable on the ground of:
o: Irrationality (Wednesbury unreasonableness) and procedural impropriety, since no reasonable authority could so act and no fair procedure was followed
The authority's lack of jurisdiction over streets
questions.e: A blanket ban with no material or rationale is Wednesbury-unreasonable — so absurd that no sensible authority could reach it — and the absence of any hearing adds procedural impropriety, both classic judicial review grounds.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The doctrine of legitimate expectation protects a substantive or procedural benefit a person reasonably expects from consistent past practice or a promise, as recognised in Navjyoti Co-operative Group Housing Society v. Union of India (1992). An authority has for years renewed licences routinely on simple application, then suddenly refuses renewal without reason or hearing. Under the stated principle:
o: The licensee has no remedy because licences are privileges
The licensee's legitimate expectation of fair procedure entitles him to a hearing before refusal
Legitimate expectation creates an absolute right to renewal
The doctrine applies only to government employees
questions.e: Navjyoti (1992) and subsequent cases hold that consistent past practice can generate a legitimate expectation of procedural fairness; while it does not guarantee the substantive outcome, it entitles the affected person to be heard.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Article 323B permits tribunals for specified matters, and in L. Chandra Kumar v. Union of India (1997), the Supreme Court held tribunal decisions subject to High Court judicial review under Articles 226/227. A statute bars all courts, including High Courts, from reviewing a tribunal's orders. Under the stated principle:
o: The ouster is unconstitutional because L. Chandra Kumar held the High Courts' Articles 226/227 power to be part of the basic structure
The ouster is valid because tribunals are efficient
Tribunals are not courts at all
Only the Supreme Court can review tribunals
questions.e: L. Chandra Kumar (1997) held that judicial review by High Courts under Articles 226 and 227 is part of the basic structure; clauses excluding it are unconstitutional, though parties must approach the tribunal first.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Natural justice has two pillars: audi alteram partem (hear the other side) and nemo judex in causa sua (no one a judge in his own cause). In A.K. Kraipak v. Union of India (1970), the Court extended natural justice to administrative decisions affecting rights. A university cancels a student's admission for alleged fraud without any notice or hearing. Under the stated principle:
o: The cancellation violates audi alteram partem and is liable to be quashed, since decisions affecting rights attract natural justice even when labelled administrative
The cancellation stands because admissions are administrative
Hearings are required only in criminal cases
The student must first pay the fees
questions.e: A.K. Kraipak (1970) demolished the rigid judicial/quasi-judicial vs administrative divide: wherever an administrative decision visits civil consequences, natural justice — at minimum a fair hearing — must be observed.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 26(1) of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 32(1) of the Indian Evidence Act) makes statements by persons who cannot be called as witnesses relevant when they relate to the cause of death. In Pakala Narayana Swami v. Emperor (1939), the Privy Council held a dying declaration admissible if it relates to the circumstances of the transaction resulting in death. A victim's statement naming her attacker is recorded before she dies. Under the stated principle:
o: The statement is admissible as a dying declaration under Section 26(1) BSA, provided it relates to the cause of death or the circumstances of the transaction resulting in death
Dying declarations require corroboration in every case
Only a magistrate can record a dying declaration
questions.e: Section 26(1) BSA (IEA 32(1)) admits dying declarations relating to the cause of death; Pakala Narayana Swami requires nexus with the transaction resulting in death, and corroboration, though desirable, is not a legal mandate.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 23 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 25 of the Indian Evidence Act) bars proof of confessions made to police officers against the accused. An accused confesses to the investigating officer in the police station and later repeats the confession before a Judicial Magistrate. Under the stated principle:
o: The confession to the police officer is inadmissible under Section 23 BSA, but the judicial confession before the Magistrate is admissible if voluntary
Confessions to police are admissible if a witness signs them
The judicial confession is inadmissible because it repeats the first
questions.e: Section 23 BSA imposes a blanket bar on confessions to police officers; a subsequent confession recorded by a Judicial Magistrate is admissible if voluntary and procedurally proper, independent of the earlier tainted one.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The proviso to Section 23(2) BSA (corresponding to Section 27 of the Indian Evidence Act) permits proof of information leading to discovery of a fact, even from a person in police custody. In Pulukuri Kottaya v. Emperor (1947), the Privy Council limited this to the distinctly discovered fact. An accused in custody reveals where he hid the weapon, which is recovered. Under the stated principle:
o: Only so much of the information as relates distinctly to the fact thereby discovered — the weapon's location and recovery — is admissible
Nothing said in custody is ever admissible
The weapon is inadmissible as evidence
questions.e: Pulukuri Kottaya (1947) confined Section 27 (now the proviso to Section 23(2) BSA) to the distinctly discovered fact; the admissible portion is the information leading to discovery, not the whole narrative.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 39 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 45 of the Indian Evidence Act) makes expert opinion relevant on points of foreign law, science, art, identity of handwriting or finger impressions. In Murari Lal v. State of M.P. (1980), the Court held expert opinion is advisory, not conclusive. A handwriting expert opines a signature is forged. Under the stated principle:
o: The court must accept the expert's opinion as conclusive
Expert opinion is inadmissible in criminal trials
The expert's opinion under Section 39 BSA is relevant but advisory; the court may also compare the writing itself and must reach its own conclusion
questions.e: Murari Lal (1980) held expert opinion under Section 45 (now Section 39 BSA) is relevant but not conclusive; courts must apply their own mind and may corroborate with direct comparison.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 104 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 101 of the Indian Evidence Act) places the burden of proving a fact on whoever asserts its existence. The prosecution alleges the accused committed murder. Under the stated principle:
o: The accused must prove his innocence
The burden shifts to the accused once charges are framed
The prosecution bears the burden of proving guilt beyond reasonable doubt throughout the trial, per Section 104 BSA
Burden of proof applies only in civil cases
questions.e: Section 104 BSA (IEA 101) embodies the presumption of innocence: the prosecution must prove every element of the offence beyond reasonable doubt; the burden never shifts to the accused to prove innocence.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 109 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act) provides that when a fact is especially within the knowledge of a person, the burden of proving it lies on him. A wife is found dead in the matrimonial home where only the husband was present. Under the stated principle:
o: The husband has no burden at all
Section 109 abolishes the presumption of innocence
The husband must explain the circumstances of the death under Section 109 BSA, though the prosecution must first establish the foundational facts
The husband must prove murder by someone else
questions.e: Section 109 BSA (IEA 106) requires the person with special knowledge to explain; in custodial-death contexts it casts an explanatory burden on the husband, but the prosecution must first prove the death occurred in those circumstances.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 118 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 113B of the Indian Evidence Act) raises a presumption as to dowry death where a woman dies within seven years of marriage under abnormal circumstances after cruelty for dowry. A woman dies by burns within three years of marriage; evidence shows dowry harassment soon before death. Under the stated principle:
o: No presumption arises because the death was by burns
The presumption applies only after ten years of marriage
The court shall presume dowry death under Section 118 BSA, shifting the burden to the accused to rebut
questions.e: Section 118 BSA (IEA 113B) mandates the 'shall presume' standard once its ingredients — death within seven years, cruelty/harassment for dowry soon before death — are proved, casting the rebuttal burden on the accused.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (corresponding to Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act) governs admissibility of electronic records. In Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kishanrao Gorantyal (2020), the Supreme Court held the Section 65B(4) certificate is a condition precedent. The prosecution seeks to prove CCTV footage without any certificate. Under the stated principle:
o: The footage is admissible without formalities
The electronic record is inadmissible without the Section 63 BSA certificate, which Arjun Panditrao made a condition precedent for secondary electronic evidence
Oral testimony about the footage suffices instead
The certificate is needed only for emails
questions.e: Arjun Panditrao (2020) held the certificate under Section 65B(4) (now Section 63 BSA) mandatory for admissibility of secondary electronic records; without it, the footage cannot be received in evidence.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 6(a) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 bars transfer of a spes successionis — the chance of an heir succeeding to an estate. A son, expecting to inherit his father's property, sells his 'expected share' to a buyer. Under the stated principle:
o: The sale is valid because expectations can be sold
The transfer is void under Section 6(a) TPA, as a mere chance of succession cannot be transferred
The sale is valid if registered
Spes successionis can be transferred with the father's consent
questions.e: Section 6(a) TPA prohibits transfer of spes successionis; an heir apparent's expected inheritance is a mere possibility that cannot be conveyed, and any such transfer is void.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 14 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 embodies the rule against perpetuity: vesting cannot be postponed beyond lives in being plus 18 years (plus gestation). A testator creates a trust vesting property in his great-great-grandchildren on terms postponing vesting for 100 years. Under the stated principle:
o: The disposition violates Section 14's rule against perpetuity and the remote vesting fails
The disposition is valid because wills are exempt
The rule applies only to Muslim transfers
Perpetuity is allowed for private trusts
questions.e: Section 14 TPA voids dispositions postponing vesting beyond the perpetuity period (lives in being plus eighteen years); remote vesting beyond that is void, protecting alienability.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 41 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 protects a transferee from an ostensible owner where the real owner allows another to hold himself out as owner and the transferee acts in good faith after reasonable care. In Ramcoomar Koondoo v. Macqueen (1872), the Privy Council required the transferor's apparent authority to be with the real owner's consent. A buyer purchases from a person the owner knowingly allowed to appear as owner. Under the stated principle:
o: The sale is void because only real owners can sell
Ostensible ownership applies only to gifts
The buyer is protected under Section 41 as a bona fide transferee from an ostensible owner
The buyer's good faith is irrelevant
questions.e: Section 41 TPA, per Ramcoomar Koondoo, protects bona fide purchasers from ostensible owners where the real owner's conduct created the appearance of authority and the transferee exercised reasonable care.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (part performance) can protect a transferee's possession, but since the 2001 amendment the underlying contract must be registered. In Suraj Lamp & Industries v. State of Haryana (2011), the Supreme Court held that GPA, sale-agreement and will transactions do not convey title. A buyer in possession under an unregistered agreement to sell executed in 2020 claims ownership. Under the stated principle:
o: The buyer is the full owner
The buyer gets no title — Suraj Lamp holds that unregistered GPA/agreement transfers do not convey ownership, and Section 53A cannot protect possession under a post-2001 unregistered contract
Registration is optional for urban property
questions.e: Suraj Lamp (2011) held that SA/GPA/will transactions do not transfer title; title passes only by a registered deed under Section 54 TPA and Sections 17/49 of the Registration Act. After the 2001 amendment, Section 53A protection also requires a registered contract, so an unregistered 2020 agreement confers neither title nor Section 53A protection.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 52 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 codifies lis pendens: property under litigation cannot be transferred so as to affect the rights of parties to the suit. During a pending title suit, the defendant sells the disputed land to a third party. Under the stated principle:
o: The sale defeats the plaintiff's claim
Lis pendens applies only to criminal cases
The sale is valid if the buyer paid full price
The purchaser is bound by the decree under Section 52's doctrine of lis pendens, whether or not he knew of the suit
questions.e: Section 52 TPA provides that pendente lite transfers are subject to the litigation's outcome; the purchaser takes subject to the decree, and knowledge of the suit is irrelevant.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: In Indore Development Authority v. Manoharlal (2020), a Constitution Bench interpreted Section 24(2) of the Right to Fair Compensation Act, 2013, holding acquisition lapses only where the government neither took possession nor paid compensation for five years or more. Land was acquired in 2010; compensation was paid but possession remained with the owner till 2019. Under the stated principle:
o: The acquisition did not lapse — Indore Development Authority held lapse under Section 24(2) requires both non-payment of compensation AND non-taking of possession for five years
The acquisition lapsed because possession was not taken
Lapse is automatic after two years
questions.e: The 2020 Constitution Bench held Section 24(2) lapse needs the twin failure — neither compensation paid nor possession taken — for five years; payment of compensation alone saves the acquisition, overruling Pune Municipal Corporation (2014).

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: In Salomon v. Salomon & Co. Ltd. (1897), the House of Lords held a duly incorporated company is a separate legal person distinct from its members, even if one person holds nearly all shares. In LIC v. Escorts Ltd. (1986), the Supreme Court accepted the principle while recognising veil-lifting in exceptional cases. A creditor of a one-person company seeks to attach the shareholder's personal assets for the company's debt. Under the stated principle:
o: The shareholder is automatically liable because he owns the company
The company and shareholder are separate persons under Salomon; the creditor cannot reach personal assets unless a veil-lifting ground like fraud or sham is established
One-person companies have no separate personality
The creditor must first dissolve the company
questions.e: Salomon establishes separate corporate personality; shareholders are not liable for company debts merely by ownership — the veil is lifted only on established grounds such as fraud, sham, or statutory provision.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The indoor management rule in Royal British Bank v. Turquand (1856) protects outsiders dealing with a company in good faith, who may assume internal procedures were followed. Its exceptions include forgery and knowledge of irregularity. A bank lends to a company on a board resolution later found to lack quorum, the bank having no notice of the defect. Under the stated principle:
o: The bank is protected by the Turquand rule as a bona fide outsider entitled to assume internal regularity
The loan is void because the resolution lacked quorum
The directors are personally liable to the bank
questions.e: The Turquand rule protects good-faith outsiders who may presume internal formalities were complied with; the company cannot defeat the transaction by pointing to internal irregularities unknown to the outsider.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: The ultra vires doctrine (Ashbury Railway Carriage Co. v. Riche, 1875) holds acts beyond the objects clause void and incapable of ratification. Under the Companies Act, 2013, Section 4(1)(c) requires the memorandum to state the objects. A company incorporated for textiles guarantees a film production loan, wholly outside its objects. Under the stated principle:
o: The guarantee is ultra vires the memorandum and void, incapable of ratification even by all shareholders
The guarantee is valid if shareholders approve it
Ultra vires no longer exists under the 2013 Act
The guarantee is valid because companies have implied powers
questions.e: Ashbury Railway holds ultra vires acts void ab initio and unratifiable; Section 4(1)(c) preserves the objects clause as the company's capacity boundary, so acts beyond it cannot bind the company.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013 mandates CSR for companies meeting specified net worth, turnover or net profit thresholds: the board must spend 2% of average net profits of the preceding three financial years on Schedule VII activities. A qualifying company spends only 0.5% and discloses nothing. Under the stated principle:
o: The company violates Section 135; it must spend 2% of average net profits of the last three years — unspent amounts for ongoing projects go to a special Unspent CSR Account within 30 days of the financial year's end, other unspent amounts to a Schedule VII fund within six months, with reasons disclosed in the board's report
No consequence follows because CSR is voluntary
CSR applies only to public sector companies
The 2% is computed on current-year turnover
questions.e: Section 135 makes CSR mandatory for covered companies at 2% of average net profits of the last three financial years. Unspent amounts relating to ongoing projects must be transferred to a special Unspent CSR Account within 30 days of the year's end and spent within three years; other unspent amounts go to a Schedule VII fund within six months, with the board's report explaining the shortfall.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 68 of the Companies Act, 2013 permits buy-back of shares subject to caps: not more than 25% of paid-up capital and free reserves, with post-buy-back debt not exceeding twice capital and free reserves. A company proposes a 40% buy-back funded by fresh borrowing that would treble its debt-equity ratio. Under the stated principle:
o: The buy-back is valid with board approval
Buy-backs are prohibited for listed companies
The proposal violates Section 68's 25% cap and the 2:1 debt-equity limit and cannot proceed
Shareholder approval cures any cap violation
questions.e: Section 68 imposes twin quantitative safeguards — the 25% ceiling and the 2:1 post-buy-back debt-equity ratio — precisely to prevent capital erosion through excessive buy-backs.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 2(62) of the Companies Act, 2013 defines a One Person Company as having only one member, and Section 3(1)(c) permits its formation with a nominee for succession. An entrepreneur wants limited liability without a co-founder. Under the stated principle:
o: He must find at least one more member
OPCs are available only to foreign nationals
He may incorporate an OPC under Sections 2(62) and 3(1)(c) with a single member and a nominee to take over on death or incapacity
questions.e: The 2013 Act introduced the OPC precisely to give solo entrepreneurs corporate limited liability; the nominee mechanism in Section 3(1)(c) ensures perpetual succession on the member's death or incapacity.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Sections 241-244 of the Companies Act, 2013 allow members to seek relief for oppression and mismanagement; Section 244 requires, for a company having share capital, 100 members or one-tenth of the total membership, whichever is less. Two hundred members of a 1,000-member company allege the majority is siphoning funds. Under the stated principle:
o: They cannot apply because they hold only 5% of shares
They meet Section 244's threshold — 200 exceeds both 100 members and one-tenth of 1,000
Oppression petitions lie only before civil courts
questions.e: Section 244(1)(a) requires 100 members or one-tenth of the total membership, whichever is less; here one-tenth of 1,000 is 100, and 200 applicants clear the threshold. The Tribunal may also waive the requirement on application under the proviso.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: Passage: Section 35 of the Companies Act, 2013 imposes civil liability for misstatements in a prospectus on directors, promoters and experts; Derry v. Peek (1889) set the common-law deceit standard requiring fraud. Investors lose money on shares bought on a prospectus containing false profit figures the directors knew were inflated. Under the stated principle:
o: The directors face no liability because markets are risky
The investors can claim compensation under Section 35 for the misstatement, and knowingly false statements also attract Derry v. Peek fraud liability
Prospectus liability applies only to unlisted companies
questions.e: Section 35 creates statutory civil liability for prospectus misstatements; where directors knew the figures were false, Derry v. Peek fraud adds common-law deceit liability — knowledge of falsity is the crux.

questions.subject: Preventive detention
questions.q: Preventive detention under the NSA differs from punitive detention because:
o: It aims to prevent anticipated harm rather than punish a committed offence

AT-1 bonds cannot be issued by private banks
The RBI must approve all bond write-downs retrospectively
questions.e: Decided 15 October 2026 by Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih, the judgment dismissed the appeals and left the Bombay High Court's setting aside of the Rs. 8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-down undisturbed.

questions.subject: IBC
questions.q: The October 2026 Supreme Court ruling in the GST/IBC limitation case (2026 INSC 1121) concerned which provision of the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code?
questions.e: The Court dismissed the GST department's appeal as time-barred, examining the limitation requirements under Section 62 of the IBC read with Section 238-A and Section 12(2) of the Limitation Act, 1963 (Civil Appeal No. 7882 of 2023).

questions.subject: Service law
questions.q: In Irfan Ahmad Hakak v. UT of Jammu and Kashmir (October 2026), the Supreme Court held that ambiguity in the prescribed qualification should be:
o: Construed to the benefit of the candidate
Left to the high court's discretion
questions.e: A bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar held that any ambiguity or vagueness in the prescribed qualification should be construed to the benefit of the candidate, setting aside high court judgments that had denied Hakak the Librarian post.

questions.subject: CLAT
questions.q: What is the application fee for CLAT 2027 for General/OBC/NRI/PIO/OCI candidates?
questions.e: The Consortium of NLUs notified a fee of Rs 4,000 for General/OBC/NRI/PIO/OCI candidates and Rs 3,500 for SC/ST/BPL/PwD candidates for CLAT 2027.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: When will the CLAT 2027 examination be held, and at what timing?
questions.e: CLAT 2027 is on Sunday, 6 December 2026, from 2 PM to 4 PM (PwD candidates till 4:40 PM), held offline across India; registration closed on 31 October 2026.

questions.subject: Legal reasoning
questions.q: What is the question count and marking scheme of the CLAT UG paper?
questions.e: The CLAT UG paper has 120 multiple-choice questions for 120 marks, to be answered in 2 hours, with 0.25 marks deducted for every wrong answer.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The Supreme Court's 17 October 2026 judgment declaring internet access a fundamental right of every individual, including children, was delivered by a Bench comprising:
o: Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih
Justices J. B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran
Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe
Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar
questions.e: Justices J. B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held internet access a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a), extending it expressly to children.

questions.subject: Judiciary
questions.q: 2026 INSC 1132 is the citation of which October 2026 Supreme Court judgment?
o: The Yes Bank AT-1 bonds judgment setting aside the Rs 8,415 crore write-down
questions.e: Yes Bank Ltd. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd., 2026 INSC 1132, decided 15 October 2026, set aside the Rs 8,415 crore AT-1 write-down.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 punishes:
o: Furnishing false information or concealing facts in election affidavits
questions.e: Section 125A penalises candidates who provide false information, conceal details, or fail to make mandatory disclosures in nomination papers or affidavits — and the Supreme Court held on 16 October 2026 that private citizens can complain of such offences.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: The Supreme Court's 17 October 2026 judgment holding that the government cannot accept temple land as a gift turned on which statute?
o: Tamil Nadu Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1959
questions.e: The transfer of Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple land was held to violate the TN HR&CE Act, 1959; the 2017 gift deed was declared illegal.

questions.subject: Constitution
questions.q: In its 15 October 2026 ruling on conversion and reservation, the Supreme Court discussed affirmative action under which Article?
questions.e: The Court held a convert from Hinduism to Islam cannot claim Backward Class Muslim status merely on pre-conversion social identity under Article 16(4), upholding the Madras High Court's striking down of a 2024 Tamil Nadu GO.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: CLAT 2027 will be conducted on which date and in which mode?
questions.e: CLAT 2027 is scheduled for Sunday, 6 December 2026, from 2 PM to 4 PM in offline mode.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: What is the minimum Class 12 percentage required for the CLAT 2027 UG programme (SC/ST candidates in brackets)?
questions.e: UG eligibility is 45% in Class 12 (40% for SC/ST/PwD); PG needs 50% in LLB (45% for SC/ST).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: What is the CLAT 2027 application fee for General/OBC and SC/ST/BPL/PwD candidates respectively?
questions.e: The fee is Rs 4,000 for General/OBC and Rs 3,500 for SC/ST/BPL/PwD candidates; the deadline is 31 October 2026, 11:59 PM.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: How many Junior Court Attendant posts did the Supreme Court of India advertise in October 2026?
questions.e: The Supreme Court's Junior Court Attendant Recruitment 2026 (Advt F.3/2026-SC (RC), dated 15 October 2026) offers 130 posts (Level 3, Rs 21,700-69,100); applications run 4-25 November 2026 on sci.gov.in.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Supreme Court's Senior Personal Assistant Recruitment 2026 (65 posts) has which application window?
questions.e: The 65 Senior Personal Assistant posts (Advt F.6/11/SPA/2026-SC (RC), dated 12 October 2026) have online applications from 20 October to 10 November 2026 (11:55 PM).

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: For the Supreme Court's Senior Personal Assistant posts (2026), the prescribed English shorthand speed is:
questions.e: Candidates need a degree, English shorthand at 110 w.p.m., and computer typing at 40 w.p.m.; age 18-30 as on 1 October 2026; pay Level 8 (Rs 47,600-1,51,100).

questions.subject: Insolvency Law
questions.q: In the 14 October 2026 ruling in Assistant Commissioner of Central Tax v. Sreenivasa Rao Ravinuthala (concerning Samyu Glass Private Limited), the Supreme Court held that:
o: The Revenue's appeal under Section 62 of the IBC was barred by limitation
NCLAT orders can never be appealed to the Supreme Court
Resolution plans cannot be approved after 330 days
The IBC limitation period is five years
questions.e: The Court dismissed the Revenue's appeal as barred by limitation, upholding the NCLAT (Chennai) order of 2 August 2023 that had confirmed the resolution plan for Samyu Glass approved by the NCLT, Hyderabad on 13 August 2021.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: In Secretary to Government v. Sameer Ahamed N. (2026 INSC 1129, decided 15 October 2026), the Supreme Court held that:
o: A person converted from the Hindu social order to Islam cannot claim reservation under Article 16(4) solely on pre-conversion social backwardness
Converts to Islam are entitled to Scheduled Caste reservation
All reservation for Muslim communities was abolished
Article 16(4) applies identically to all religious converts
questions.e: The Bench (Justices P. K. Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar) held conversion to a different faith does not determine entry into a notified Backward Class Muslim community, and upheld the Madras High Court's setting aside of Tamil Nadu's 2024 order on certificates for converts.

questions.subject: Constitutional & Electoral Law
questions.q: Per the Supreme Court's October 2026 ruling, who can file a criminal complaint under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 for a false election affidavit?
questions.e: The SC bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu (16 Oct 2026) held that private individuals can file criminal complaints under Section 125A RPA — Section 195(1) CrPC's requirement of a public servant's complaint does not cover 125A (inserted 2002; Section 195 amended 2006; Parliament's omission deliberate).

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: Which body fixes the number of judges of the Supreme Court of India?
questions.e: Under Article 124(1), the number of Supreme Court judges is fixed by Parliament by law — the 2026 amendment raised the sanctioned strength from 34 to 38 (including the CJI); it is not a constitutional-amendment matter.

questions.subject: Labour & Service Law
questions.q: In the Supreme Court's 6 October 2026 daily-wager increment ruling, under which year's Gujarat government resolution had the workers been treated as permanent employees?
questions.e: In Chhaganbhai Kohyabhai Pateliya v. State of Gujarat (2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1020, decided 6 Oct 2026), the Court held that daily-wage skilled workers treated as permanent employees under the 1988 Gujarat government resolution (after ten years' service) cannot be denied the annual increment falling due after retirement merely because of their original daily-wage engagement.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: Which constitutional provision did the Supreme Court invoke in its October 2026 ruling on the right to protest?
questions.e: The bench headed by CJI Surya Kant (9 Oct 2026) held that restrictions on protest must be proportionate, remarking authorities 'can't shut down an entire city' — the right flows from Article 19(1)(b) (assemble peaceably and without arms).

questions.subject: Legal Education
questions.q: Which body defended mandatory attendance norms for law students before the Supreme Court in October 2026?
questions.e: The Bar Council of India (BCI), along with premier law schools, argued before the Supreme Court (bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta, which reserved its verdict on 7 Oct 2026) that diluting mandatory attendance norms degrades academic discipline and professional standards.

questions.subject: CLAT
questions.q: CLAT 2027 is scheduled to be held on which date and time?
questions.e: The Consortium of NLUs fixed CLAT 2027 for 6 December 2026 (2-4 PM); applications are open until 31 October 2026.

questions.subject: CLAT
questions.q: Applications for CLAT 2027 are open until which date?
questions.e: CLAT 2027 applications close on 31 October 2026 for the 6 December 2026 exam.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: In September 2026 the Rajasthan High Court rejected a CLAT candidate's plea to change her reservation category after results. What was the court's key reasoning?
o: The correction window (till 9 Nov 2025) was not availed and post-result change is an afterthought disturbing the merit list
questions.e: The Court held that the correction window till 9 November 2025 was not availed, counselling began 7 January 2026, and the selection process is a continuum where the category once opted is binding; post-result correction would unsettle the merit list.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: As per NIRF 2025 rankings, which is the No. 1 ranked law school in India?
questions.e: NIRF 2025: NLSIU Bangalore ranked No. 1, NLU Delhi No. 2, NLU Kolkata No. 4 among law institutions.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: What deadline did the Supreme Court set on 21 October 2026 for digitising all police stations?
questions.e: In S. Ganesh vs State of Tamil Nadu (21 Oct 2026), Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah & R. Mahadevan gave states/UTs one month to equip every police station with digitisation hardware and internet, calling unconnected stations “absolutely unacceptable.” FIRs must go to CCTNS; CWCs must also be digitised.

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: Under which provisions did the SC recognise internet access as a fundamental right (Oct 2026)?
questions.e: Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish (2026 INSC 1149, 15 Oct 2026): the right to access and use the internet is a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a) — “our children, irrespective of their age, enjoy the same rights.”

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: The SC's October 2026 internet-rights judgment directed stronger action against which online harm?
o: Child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM)
questions.e: The Court directed stronger mechanisms to detect and remove child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) from social media and online services — while holding that children's safety and their freedom “are not at odds with each other.”

questions.subject: Constitutional Law
questions.q: The SC's 15 Oct 2026 ruling on religious converts and backward-class status turned on which Article?
questions.e: Upholding the Madras HC, the SC (15 Oct 2026) held that conversion to a non-Hindu order does not carry pre-conversion social status with it — affirmative action under Article 16(4) (reservation in public employment) cannot be claimed on that basis.

questions.subject: Media Law
questions.q: The MIB's 21 Oct 2026 advisory asks TV channels to comply with the Programme Code under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act of which year?
questions.e: The MIB advisory of 21 October 2026 requires private satellite TV channels to keep AI in an assistive role in news production and to comply with the Programme Code under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 (and the 1994 Rules).

questions.subject: Election Law
questions.q: The SC's 12 Oct 2026 clarification on Form 6 arose from which earlier case?
questions.e: The Court clarified (12 Oct 2026) that the May 27 judgment concerned only the legality of the pilot Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in Bihar; the modified Form 6 came later (July) and was “neither approved nor disapproved.” It will be examined now.

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: The Consortium of National Law Universities released the CLAT 2027 notification on:
questions.e: The CLAT 2027 notification was released on 15 October 2026, opening registrations for admission to undergraduate BA LLB (Hons) and postgraduate LLM programmes at 24 National Law Universities.

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: What is the last date to register for CLAT 2027?
questions.e: Registration closes on 31 October 2026 (11:59 PM) via consortiumofnlus.ac.in; the exam is on 6 December 2026 (2:00–4:00 PM).

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: AILET 2027 will be conducted on 13 December 2026. What is its application deadline?
questions.e: AILET 2027 (conducted by NLU Delhi, for NLU Delhi admissions only): apply by 10 November 2026; exam on 13 December 2026; 150 questions across three sections, with 70 on Logical Reasoning.

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: What is the CLAT 2027 application fee for general-category candidates?
questions.e: Rs 4,000 for general candidates; Rs 3,500 for SC/ST/BPL candidates. UG eligibility: Class 12 with 45% (40% for SC/ST).

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: As per the CLAT 2027 pattern, the marking scheme is:
questions.e: CLAT marking: +1 for each correct answer, -0.25 for each incorrect answer. CLAT UG 2027 has 120 questions across five sections including Legal Reasoning and Quantitative Techniques (2 hours).

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: CLAT 2027 applications close on 31 October 2026. The examination will be held on:
questions.e: CLAT 2027 is on Sunday, 6 December 2026, 2–4 PM, in offline pen-and-paper mode across centres in India.

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about the CLAT 2027 pattern?
o: 120 questions in 2 hours with +1/−0.25, unchanged this cycle
Online CBT with no negative marking
questions.e: CLAT 2027 UG: 120 questions, 2 hours, +1/−0.25; the syllabus, sections and pattern are unchanged this cycle — reforms apply from CLAT 2028.

questions.subject: Legal GK
questions.q: Eligibility for CLAT 2027 UG requires Class 12 with:
questions.e: UG eligibility: 45% in Class 12 (40% for SC/ST/PwD); no upper age limit.

questions.subject: Judiciary
questions.q: The High Court of Andhra Pradesh's 2026 Civil Judge (Junior Division) recruitment offers how many vacancies, and what is the last date?
questions.e: 119 vacancies — 96 under Direct Recruitment and 23 under Recruitment by Transfer; last date 26.10.2026.

questions.subject: Judiciary
questions.q: For the AP Civil Judge (Junior Division) direct recruitment 2026, the key eligibility condition is:
o: Law degree obtained in the preceding one year as on the notification date
questions.e: Direct recruitment requires candidates to have obtained their law degree in the preceding one year as on the notification date.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: The Supreme Court of India's Junior Court Assistant recruitment (250 posts) has its last date on:
questions.e: Applications for 250 Junior Court Assistant posts (Level 6, ₹35,400) in the Supreme Court of India close at 11:55 pm on 28 October 2026.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.q: How many Senior Personal Assistant posts did the Supreme Court of India advertise, closing 10 November 2026?
questions.e: The Supreme Court advertised 65 Senior Personal Assistant posts (Level 8, ₹47,600), closing 10 November 2026, plus 20 Court Master (Shorthand) posts closing 15 November 2026.

questions.subject: Legal Current Affairs
questions.q: Which bodies will enforce the EU AI Act in Italy under Legislative Decree No. 179 (23 October 2026)?
o: The Agency for Digital Italy (AgID) and the National Cybersecurity Agency (ACN)
The European Court of Justice directly
questions.e: Promulgated on 7 October 2026, the decree divides supervisory and enforcement authority between AgID and ACN — a model of how EU member states are building domestic enforcement for the AI Act.

questions.subject: Legal Current Affairs
questions.q: Under Italy's Legislative Decree No. 179 implementing the EU AI Act, violations of prohibited AI practices can attract fines of up to:
o: EUR 35 million or 7% of annual global turnover
questions.e: The decree mirrors the AI Act's penalty structure at the national level: up to EUR 35 million or 7% of annual global turnover for prohibited practices, and it also establishes a regulatory sandbox for enterprises.

capsules.title: Nobel Economics 2026: Hall & Woodford
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences went to Robert E. Hall and Michael Woodford (announced 12 Oct 2026 by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences).

capsules.title: Nobel Chemistry 2026: Kagan & Soai
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry went to Henri Kagan and Kenso Soai (announced 7 Oct 2026) for the discovery of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis.

capsules.title: Nobel Literature 2026: Anne Carson
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature went to Canadian author Anne Carson (announced 8 Oct 2026) — for her bold and inventive oeuvre in dialogue with the classical tradition.

capsules.title: Nobel Physics 2026: Francis Halzen
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics went to Francis Halzen (announced 6 Oct 2026) for decisive contributions to the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos of astrophysical origin.

capsules.title: 3rd Sagarmanthan oceans dialogue held
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The 3rd Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue was held 7–9 Oct 2026 in New Delhi on the theme ‘Blue Geographies, New Aspirations: Trade, Technology, and Trust at Sea’ — 1,200 participants from ~75 countries; organised by ORF and the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

capsules.title: Ashutosh Dixit: next Chief of the Air Staff
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit will take charge as the 29th Chief of the Air Staff on 31 Oct 2026, succeeding Air Chief Marshal Amar Preet Singh (PIB, 8 Oct 2026).

capsules.title: Three HC Chief Justices elevated to Supreme Court
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — On 5 Oct 2026 the President appointed Gujarat CJ Justice Sunita Agarwal, Delhi CJ Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Telangana CJ Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh as Supreme Court judges under Article 124(2) (Ministry of Law and Justice).

capsules.title: NHRC camp sitting in Patna on 7–8 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The NHRC held a two-day open hearing and camp sitting in Patna on 7–8 Oct 2026; the full bench led by Chairperson Justice V Ramasubramanian heard pending Bihar cases.

capsules.title: Press Council of India reconstituted
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The Centre selected 13 new journalist members for the Press Council of India on 8 Oct 2026 — six working journalists under the editors' category and seven other working journalists.

capsules.title: Bihar MLC polls: 8 seats on 23 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — Biennial elections to 8 Bihar Legislative Council seats (4 Graduates', 4 Teachers') will be held on 23 Oct 2026; 164 candidates in fray; counting on 27 Oct (CEO Bihar).

capsules.title: Supreme Court Junior Court Assistant 2026: apply by 28 Oct
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court's Junior Court Assistant 2026 advertisement (dated 30 Sep 2026) is live on sci.gov.in; ~250 tentative Group-B posts, applications 7–28 Oct 2026.

capsules.title: SC special hearing on Delhi detentions (11 Oct)
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court fixed a special Sunday hearing on 11 Oct for pleas challenging mass detentions and the transit shutdown in Delhi during protests against the Chief Election Commissioner (The Hindu, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.title: UN rights body flags Delhi detentions
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The UN Human Rights Office (OHCHR) said it was ‘concerned’ by reports of ‘mass detentions’ at the Delhi protests against the Chief Election Commissioner; the government rejected the statement (The Hindu, 11 Oct 2026).

capsules.title: US sanctions ICC after Peace Nobel
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — Hours after former ICC judge Navi Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize, the US imposed financial sanctions on the International Criminal Court (reported 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.title: Nobel Peace Prize 2026: Navi Pillay
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The Norwegian Nobel Committee awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize to South African jurist Navi Pillay for her work to ensure war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

capsules.title: Defence Secretary to visit Cyprus, Greece
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — The Defence Secretary will visit Cyprus and Greece from 12–15 Oct 2026 (PIB, 10 Oct 2026).

capsules.title: UPI-MDR from 15 Oct: 0.4% above ₹2,000
capsules.body: 11 Oct 2026 — From 15 Oct 2026, specified UPI merchant payments above ₹2,000 carry 0.4% MDR (capped at ₹300); person-to-person transfers stay free.

capsules.title: SIR: 14 lakh added to Bihar rolls
capsules.body: Oct 2026 — Nearly 14 lakh voters were added to Bihar's electoral rolls after the Special Intensive Revision (18.7 lakh Form-6 applications, ~14 lakh enrolments) — key material for electoral-law questions on roll revision and the right to vote.

capsules.title: Agitation: CEC resignation demand
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The Bihar Congress launched a phased agitation demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation and SIR rollback — landmark material on the Election Commission's independence, appointment and accountability.

capsules.title: Constitution Day march planned
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The agitation's culminating 'Delhi Chalo' march is planned for Constitution Day (26 November) — the day the Constitution was adopted in 1949, relevant for constitutional-history questions.

capsules.title: Jan Suraaj: EC 'failed to ensure transparency'
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor alleged the EC 'failed to ensure transparency' in Bihar's polls — a free-and-fair-elections jurisprudence data point.

capsules.title: Delhi protest: SIR rollback demand
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The CJP's Jantar Mantar protest demanded the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and rollback of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls — landmark material for constitutional-law questions on the Election Commission.

capsules.title: Preventive detention scale: 15,000+
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Over 15,000 protesters were detained across Delhi amid the anti-CEC protest; the MHA directed states to prevent mobilisation — relevant for preventive-detention and public-order jurisprudence.

capsules.title: GST decriminalisation: arrest powers scrapped
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — The 57th GST Council scrapped arrest powers under GST and raised the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore — key for economic-offences and tax-law questions.

capsules.title: GST penalty cut: Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — The general penalty under GST was cut from Rs 25,000 to Rs 10,000 — a proportionality point for administrative-law answers.

capsules.title: Nobel Peace 2026: Navi Pillay
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay, 85, won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize 'for her efforts to promote peace and international law'. The South African jurist of Indian Tamil origin served as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (2008–14) and as a judge of the International Criminal Court — landmark material for international-law questions.

capsules.title: Bihar MLC polls: 164 candidates, voting 23 Oct
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Biennial elections to 8 Bihar Legislative Council seats (4 Graduates' + 4 Teachers' constituencies) will be held on 23 October 2026 with 164 candidates in the fray; counting is on 27 October. The state announced special casual leave for employee-voters in the poll-bound constituencies.

capsules.title: RBI: dollar window for oil firms, ETCD curbs
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — The RBI opened a special dollar window for Indian Oil, HPCL and BPCL (from 12 Oct), cut the rupee exchange-traded derivative limit to $5 million from $100 million, and ordered a 20% foreign exchange risk reserve on rupee derivative notionals — relevant for economic-law and FEMA-adjacent questions.

capsules.title: Bihar MSME Policy 2026
capsules.body: 10 Oct 2026 — Bihar launched its MSME Policy 2026 targeting 1 crore families self-reliant through entrepreneurship; 45,000 entrepreneurs are being developed (Rs 3,500 crore), and 25–40% of government procurement will come from in-state products.

capsules.title: PM's global cyber-fraud & deepfake framework
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — PM Narendra Modi on 8 Oct called for a global framework to tackle cross-border cyber fraud and the growing threat of deepfakes, urging governments, technology companies, telecom operators and financial institutions to build a mechanism that stops such frauds before they reach people.

capsules.title: Rajghat sit-in: SIR and the ECI
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — INDIA bloc leaders staged a peaceful sit-in at Rajghat on 8 Oct — the third day of protests — demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged ‘vote chori’ and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained during the march to the Election Commission earlier in the week.

capsules.title: Cancer drugs: 30% trade-margin cap
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The Centre has decided to cap trade margins at 30% of MRP for all non-scheduled anti-cancer drugs — 110 drugs including 35 patented medicines — which could cut MRPs by up to 70% and save patients ~₹2,500 crore a year. The NPPA approved the move in principle at its 151st meeting on 8 Oct (chaired by Manoj Joshi); a 2019 pilot on 42 drugs cut prices up to 91%, saving ₹984 crore.

capsules.title: CBI busts bank recruitment racket
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The CBI has busted an inter-state bank recruitment racket, arresting four people including a CGST inspector.

capsules.title: US suspends 8 firms from PERM
capsules.body: 9 Oct 2026 — The US Labour Department on 8 Oct suspended 8 tech majors — TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCLTech, Cognizant, Capgemini, Microsoft and Adobe — from the Permanent Labour Certification (PERM) programme, the key step in employment-based green cards, over alleged H-1B abuse. Labour Secretary Keith Sonderling said the firms had sought ‘almost three million foreign workers’ since 2009; VP JD Vance alleged Microsoft laid off 6,000 Americans in 2025 while securing 6,300 H-1B visas.

capsules.title: Rahul, Priyanka detained after EC march
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra were detained by Delhi Police on Tuesday evening after an hours-long sit-in at Akashvani Bhawan during the INDIA bloc's march to the Election Commission, demanding the resignation of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over the SIR (Special Intensive Revision) of electoral rolls.

capsules.title: Hormuz attack: India condemns
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — Eleven Indian crew members were injured after a Panama-flagged commercial vessel was hit by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz; India strongly condemned the attack on the ship.

capsules.title: Cabinet: 25 years resolution
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — The Union Cabinet passed a resolution marking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 25 years as a head of government.

capsules.title: Pre-COP31: balanced climate action
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — India urged balanced climate action at the Pre-COP31 meet and offered coastal-monitoring expertise to Pacific partners.

capsules.title: Container trains: single all-India licence
capsules.body: 7 Oct 2026 — The Centre has approved a single all-India licence for container train operators to boost rail freight.

capsules.title: Three new SC judges: the 3:30 PM oath
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Justices Sunita Agarwal (Gujarat HC Chief Justice), Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (Delhi HC Chief Justice) and Aparesh Kumar Singh (Telangana HC Chief Justice) were sworn in as Supreme Court judges at a rare 3:30 PM ceremony, with CJI Surya Kant administering the oath. The Centre had notified the appointments on 5 Oct after the collegium's 28 September recommendation. Working strength rises from 34 to 37 — one short of the sanctioned 38, raised from 34 by the Supreme Court Amendment Act, 2026. Justice Agarwal becomes the third woman judge, alongside Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Venkita Subramani Mohana.

capsules.title: Sanctioned strength 34 to 38
capsules.body: The Supreme Court Amendment Act, 2026 raised the sanctioned strength from 34 to 38; the 6 Oct oath took working strength to 37 — a live Article 124 case study on appointments.

capsules.title: Delhi HC: no SIT in 2020-riots pleas
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — The Delhi High Court rejected pleas seeking an SIT probe and FIRs against politicians over the 2020 Delhi riots. Separately, the Allahabad High Court said parents cannot force an adult daughter to live with them, and Tamil Nadu CM Vijay sought the release of 20 fishermen detained by Sri Lanka.

capsules.title: MPSC paper-leak probe panel
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis has proposed setting up a committee to examine the conduct of former and incumbent chairpersons and members of the Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) over paper leaks.

capsules.title: Tribal students detained after march
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Mumbai Police detained tribal students who had marched from Nashik to press for better hostel facilities and an inquiry, and drove them out of the city.

capsules.title: CJI: no SC approval for Form 6 changes
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — CJI Surya Kant said the Supreme Court did not approve "any" modifications to Form 6, the form voters fill to register, as a three-judge bench headed by him heard petitions against CEC Gyanesh Kumar. Separately, the Court issued notices to the Election Commission and the Centre, observing that decisions taken without unanimity or majority could be annulled, amid the Form 6 controversy.

capsules.title: SC: create fear among criminals to curb crimes against women
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court has directed police to "create fear" among criminals and goons to prevent crimes against women, stressing stronger action to ensure public safety.

capsules.title: INDIA bloc marches to the EC over alleged vote theft
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — INDIA bloc MPs are marching to the Election Commission's office today over alleged "vote theft". Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge has announced "Save Democracy" rallies in every district from 2 to 8 October, a demand that ballot papers replace EVMs, and a public meeting in Delhi on 1 November.

capsules.title: J&K: 150 Bangladeshi nationals to be deported
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Jammu and Kashmir authorities on 5 Oct said 150 Bangladeshi nationals staying illegally in the Union Territory are being deported, as part of a stepped-up drive against illegal immigration.

capsules.title: Brazil heads to presidential runoff
capsules.body: 6 Oct 2026 — Brazil's presidential election heads to a runoff after no candidate won outright in the first round: incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva faces far-right challenger Flavio Bolsonaro, son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro.

capsules.title: Nobel week begins: medicine prize to optogenetics trio
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — Karl Deisseroth (54, American), Peter Hegemann (71, German) and Georg Nagel (73, German) won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine “for discoveries concerning light-gated ion channels and optogenetics”, announced by the Nobel Assembly at Sweden's Karolinska Institute. Optogenetics lets scientists switch individual nerve cells in a living brain on or off with light; the method is used in labs worldwide to reveal neural circuits behind memory, feelings and behaviour, and is being explored to restore sight. Hegemann and Nagel discovered the light-sensitive channelrhodopsin protein in the alga Chlamydomonas; Deisseroth (Stanford) showed in 2005 that it can control nerve cells. The 12-million-Swedish-crown prize (about $1.2 million) is shared; the physics, chemistry, literature, peace and economics prizes follow this week.

capsules.title: RBI's statutory mandate in focus as MPC meets 5–7 Oct
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee began its three-day meeting today; the repo-rate decision is due on 7 October. Markets widely expect a 25 bps hike to 5.50% — which would be the first increase since February 2023, when the rate was raised to 6.50%. The repo rate has sat at 5.25% through four consecutive reviews after cumulative 125 bps cuts in 2025. Drivers: August CPI at 4.82% (third straight month above the 4% target), Brent crude near $101 a barrel, and the US Fed's recent hike. A 25 bps rise could push floating home-loan rates from 8.5% to 8.75%, adding about ₹795 a month to a ₹50 lakh, 20-year EMI.

capsules.title: Delhi AQI 187: GRAP and the CAQM's emergency toolkit
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — Delhi's air quality hit an 83-day high of 187 ('moderate') on 4 Oct and eased to 183 on 5 Oct, per the CPCB; the last higher reading was 246 on 13 July. Sixteen monitoring stations recorded 'poor' air (Mundka 273, Narela 257), and NCR cities Noida (281), Ghaziabad (248) and Faridabad (224) slipped into 'poor' too. If the AQI crosses 200, GRAP Stage 1 kicks in. CPCB bands: 0–50 good, 51–100 satisfactory, 101–200 moderate, 201–300 poor, 301–400 very poor, 401–500 severe. The IARI recorded 203 stubble-burning incidents across Punjab, UP and MP between 15 September and 3 October; Delhi saw its most polluted October start in four years.

capsules.title: Asian Games final: sporting diplomacy without handshakes
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — India defended their Asian Games men's cricket gold on 3 Oct, beating Pakistan by 19 runs in the final at Nisshin (India 211/6, Pakistan 192/6). Abhishek Sharma's 61 off 28 and Tilak Varma's unbeaten 51 off 22 powered India; Hasan Nawaz's 51-ball 96 kept Pakistan in the hunt. Shreyas Iyer won the toss and chose to bat. It was the first India–Pakistan clash at the Asian Games, and the two sides avoided the customary handshakes. The gold completes a cricket double — India's women beat Sri Lanka in the final on 22 September — and Sri Lanka took bronze, beating Bangladesh by 63 runs.

capsules.title: Stubble burning: 203 incidents in 19 days
capsules.body: The IARI recorded 203 stubble-burning incidents across Punjab, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh between 15 September and 3 October — the seasonal trigger behind Delhi's AQI spike. Farm-fire enforcement sits at the intersection of environmental law, the CAQM's directions and state machinery.

capsules.title: SARFAESI: civil courts barred — Nagarathna & Masih
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court (Justices B.V. Nagarathna and Augustine George Masih) has ruled that civil courts have no jurisdiction to entertain suits over SARFAESI recovery actions: challenges to measures under the SARFAESI Act, 2002 lie only before the Debts Recovery Tribunal or the Appellate Tribunal. Section 34 of the Act expressly bars civil courts, Section 32 shields actions taken in good faith, and Section 35 gives the Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws.

capsules.title: SC suo motu: 135-yr library, SMW(C) 21/2026
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court has taken suo motu cognisance (SMW(C) No. 21/2026, registered 3 Oct) of the proposed relocation of the 135-year-old Central Secretariat Library — over 8.5 lakh books, currently housed in Shastri Bhawan — under the Central Vista plan; a bench of Justices Sanjay Kumar and Sanjeev Sachdeva hears the matter today, 5 Oct. The Union Housing Ministry says space for the library has been earmarked under the Kartavya Path redevelopment plan.

capsules.title: SC: mandate ≠ unbridled authority (Mhatre)
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court, in State of Maharashtra v. Ramesh Sukrya Mhatre, has held that a people's mandate cannot confer unbridled authority on elected representatives; it set aside a Bombay High Court order restoring bail to four accused, directed them to surrender before the trial court by 5 Oct, and asked the Special Fast Track Court to conclude the trial expeditiously.

capsules.title: SC: circumstantial-evidence chain test (Anchla)
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court (Justices Manoj Misra and Vijay Bishnoi, judgment 1 Oct) has upheld the acquittal of Anchla alias Chanchla in a 2011 Himachal Pradesh double-murder case, holding that where a case rests on circumstantial evidence, the chain of circumstances must be complete, consistent only with the accused's guilt, and must exclude every reasonable hypothesis of innocence.

capsules.title: Uttarakhand to repeal 1873 Canal & Drainage Act
capsules.body: 5 Oct 2026 — Uttarakhand CM Pushkar Singh Dhami on 4 Oct chaired a state cabinet meeting at the NHPC complex in Banbasa, Champawat — the first ever held outside Dehradun, on the India-Nepal border. The cabinet decided to repeal the 153-year-old British-era Northern India Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 and replace it with a new state law, as part of a push to take governance to remote border areas.

capsules.title: Bhadohi renamed Sant Ravidas Nagar — district renaming
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — UP CM Yogi Adityanath renamed Bhadohi district as 'Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi', honouring the medieval saint; the announcement came at a programme launching 112 development projects worth over ₹1,340 crore. Bhadohi is famous for its carpet industry.

capsules.title: US visa bonds up to $20,000: immigration-law flashpoint
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The United States imposed visa bonds of up to $20,000 on tourist and business visa applicants from 50 countries; India is exempt, but South Asian neighbours Bangladesh, Bhutan and Nepal are covered.

capsules.title: FZ1073: UAE AG finds co-pilot attempted terrorist act
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The UAE Attorney-General said investigations into the flydubai flight FZ1073 incident found the co-pilot attempted a terrorist act; Dubai Crown Prince Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed visited Captain Smit Machchhar, the Indian pilot who saved the flight.

capsules.title: Leprosy: 3,832 children diagnosed; 2027 target
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — 3,832 children were diagnosed with leprosy in India, reported as the country works toward interrupting leprosy transmission by 2027 under the National Leprosy Eradication Programme. Leprosy (Hansen's disease) is caused by Mycobacterium leprae and is curable with multidrug therapy (dapsone, rifampicin, clofazimine).

capsules.title: MPSC: 70,000 posts vacant; Pune protest
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — Congress leader Ajay Maken backed aspirants protesting in Pune over 70,000 unfilled Maharashtra government posts; on 3 Oct, Rahul Gandhi endorsed their demand that the vacancies be filled at once, routed through his Satyagraha platform.

capsules.title: SSSC notifies 1,270 Clerk posts for Punjab District Courts
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The SSSC (under the Punjab & Haryana High Court) has notified 1,270 Clerk posts for Punjab's District Courts (Employment Notice 37C/SSSC/PB/2026, dated 3 Oct 2026): online applications run 7 Oct (4:00 PM) to 4 Nov 2026 (4:00 PM) at sssc.gov.in. Eligibility: bachelor's degree + matriculation with Punjabi + computer proficiency; selection via Computer Based Test → Computer Proficiency Test → document verification. (Notice confirmed on the official sssc.gov.in homepage; details cross-checked with independent reports.)

capsules.title: RBI MPC 5–7 Oct: first hike since Feb 2023 on the cards
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The RBI's six-member Monetary Policy Committee meets 5–7 October (decision on 7 Oct): 8 of 10 economists in a Business Standard poll expect the first rate hike since February 2023 — 25 basis points, taking the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50%. The RBI has held the repo unchanged for four straight reviews after cutting a cumulative 125 bps in 2025.

capsules.title: India 4th at Asian Games: 85 medals
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — India finished 4th at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games 2026 with 85 medals: 21 gold, 27 silver, 37 bronze. China topped with 341 medals (169 gold), hosts Japan were second with 269 (83 gold), South Korea third with 150 (39 gold). India matched Uzbekistan on 21 golds but stayed ahead on silvers. The Games close today with the closing ceremony at Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium (2:30–4 PM IST).

capsules.title: Men's hockey 5-1: LA28 quota sealed
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — India thrashed Malaysia 5-1 in the Asian Games men's hockey final on 3 Oct: captain Harmanpreet Singh scored twice (including a 12th-minute drag-flick), Hardik Singh converted a penalty stroke, and Shilanand Lakra bagged one; Malaysia's Shello Silverius replied. India's 21st gold sealed a direct LA 2028 Olympic quota and — with the women's 1-0 win over China on 2 Oct — the first-ever Asian Games where BOTH Indian teams took hockey gold.

capsules.title: Neeru Dhanda: flag bearer at today's closing ceremony
capsules.body: 4 Oct 2026 — The 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games close TODAY: the closing ceremony is at the Nagoya City Mizuho Park Athletic Stadium between 2:30 PM and 4 PM IST, with double-gold trap shooter Neeru Dhanda leading the Indian contingent as flag bearer.

capsules.title: NCW's 37-point maternity/childcare report to the Centre
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — The National Commission for Women submitted a 37-point report to the Centre (DoPT, Women & Child Development, Labour ministries): gender-neutral Child Care Leave for the private sector, mandatory paid paternity leave, and 5 lakh crèche seats by 2030 via a National Childcare Infrastructure Mission; the 730-day CCL would be split 365/365 between both working parents.

capsules.title: 700+ detained at Jantar Mantar over SIR; CEC removal demanded
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Delhi Police detained 700+ protesters at Jantar Mantar (2 Oct) demanding the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls; former Delhi CM Atishi was among those detained.

capsules.title: PM Modi speaks to flydubai Captain Machchhar; bravery award sought
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — PM Modi spoke with flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar, who saved flight FZ1073 (Dubai–Tel Aviv) after his co-pilot attacked him mid-air; the Federation of Indian Pilots has sought a National Bravery Award for him, and the co-pilot (an Omani citizen) was reportedly barred from flying in Oman.

capsules.title: CAQM: 197 inspections across NCR (8–24 Sep)
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — The Commission for Air Quality Management reviewed NCR enforcement for 8–24 September: 197 inspections were reported across the National Capital Region (Environment Ministry).

capsules.title: 28 Ladakh locations named on Survey of India map
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — The Centre formally named 28 geographical locations and features in Ladakh as per standard Survey of India map names — including Gogra and Hot Springs, areas associated with the India-China border tensions — for accurate identification and public awareness.

capsules.title: ECI extends SIR in AP and Meghalaya
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — The Election Commission extended the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) schedule for electoral rolls in Andhra Pradesh and Meghalaya.

capsules.title: Flydubai captain airlifted after cockpit attack
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar, stabbed by his co-pilot during a mid-air cockpit attack, is being airlifted to Abu Dhabi for further treatment.

capsules.title: Delhi AQI 166: worst October start in 4 years
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — Delhi recorded its most polluted start to October in four years: AQI 166.

capsules.title: GST mop-up: ₹2.04 lakh crore, +14.7%
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — September gross GST collections hit ₹2.04 lakh crore, up 14.7% year-on-year, on steady economic activity and pre-festive inventory build-up.
