capsules.title: HDFC Bank: Anup Bagchi to be CEO
capsules.body: 3 Oct 2026 — HDFC Bank, India's largest private lender, appointed Anup Bagchi as its next CEO for three years.

capsules.title: NCLT can recall fraud-based CIRP: Supreme Court
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court (Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe, judgment 30 Sep 2026) ruled the NCLT can recall admission of a corporate insolvency resolution process if founded on fraud and collusion — jurisdictional facts are conditions precedent; it may also proceed under Section 65 of the IBC.

capsules.title: SC declines stay on UPI merchant fee from 15 Oct
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — On 28 September 2026 the Supreme Court declined to stay the 0.4% UPI merchant fee (above ₹2,000) starting 15 October 2026; a CJI Surya Kant-led bench issued notice to the Centre, RBI and NPCI, giving four weeks to explain the charge's basis (Anjan Datta v. Union of India).

capsules.title: SC quashes Sambhal NSA detention; ₹10 lakh cost on UP
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court quashed the NSA detention of Sambhal-violence accused Mulla Afroz (29 Sep 2026), holding a custodial confession alone cannot ground preventive detention, and imposed a ₹10 lakh cost on the Uttar Pradesh government (Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu).

capsules.title: SC seeks middle path on firecrackers; next hearing 15 Oct
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — The Supreme Court (30 Sep 2026) said it would neither fully ban firecrackers nor allow them round the clock amid Delhi's air pollution; it ordered CPCB and the Centre to jointly test barium use and noise levels, with the next hearing on 15 October.

capsules.title: Chhattisgarh opens six open jails on Gandhi Jayanti
capsules.body: 2 Oct 2026 — Chhattisgarh opens six new open jails on Gandhi Jayanti (2 Oct), letting eligible inmates (aged 30–60, with 7+ years of a 10-year/life sentence served) work outside during daytime across Raipur, Bilaspur, Ambikapur, Durg and Jagdalpur — a prison-reform push toward reintegration.

capsules.title: SC to hear Ram Temple donation plea on 2 November
capsules.body: The Supreme Court agreed on 1 October 2026 to hear on 2 November a plea by the Akhil Bharat Hindu Mahasabha seeking legal action against former Shri Ram Janmabhooti Teerth Kshetra Trust general secretary Champat Rai and others over alleged irregularities in donations and land transactions linked to the Ayodhya Ram Temple. A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant will hear it; the plea also seeks dissolution and complete reconstitution of the Trust.

capsules.title: Calcutta HC bars prayers at mosque near airport runway on security grounds
capsules.body: The Calcutta High Court on 1 October 2026 refused permission to offer prayers in the mosque near the runway inside Kolkata airport, citing national security concerns; the recent Flydubai incident was raised during the hearing.

capsules.title: PM Modi to address UPSC Centenary Celebrations at Bharat Mandapam
capsules.body: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will participate in the Centenary Celebrations of the Union Public Service Commission — a constitutional body under Article 315 — at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, on 1 October 2026.

capsules.title: NCERT Class 9 textbook traces 'Satyamev Jayate' to Mundaka Upanishad
capsules.body: A new Class 9 social science textbook highlights how mottos of modern Indian institutions, including 'Satyamev Jayate' from the Mundaka Upanishad, originate in the Upanishads and the Mahabharata.

capsules.title: Gujarat announces 'Visisht Gujarat Garima Award' for Captain Smit Machchhar
capsules.body: The Gujarat government announced the award for the Flydubai captain who saved a plane with over 170 passengers from a crash.

capsules.title: Textile conclave in New Delhi; Giriraj Singh to inaugurate
capsules.body: New Delhi will host a textile conclave on 1 October 2026 on emerging technologies in the textile sector, to be inaugurated by Union Textile Minister Giriraj Singh.

capsules.title: SC grants Class VI one-time relief from CBSE three-language rule
capsules.body: A bench led by CJI Surya Kant extended to Class VI the relaxation already available to Classes VII–IX: no compulsory third language for 2026–27, only school-based assessment with an appearance certificate and no pass/fail; the policy itself remains under challenge with implementation from the April 2027 intake.

capsules.title: SC suggests linking unpaid traffic e-challans to electricity bills
capsules.body: Justices J.B. Pardiwala and K.V. Viswanathan noted about Rs 20,000 crore of roughly Rs 45,000 crore in traffic e-challans remains unrecovered and suggested adding unpaid challans to electricity bills so recovery follows the power connection.

capsules.title: SC asks Centre to make 18 the minimum age for social media accounts
capsules.body: Hearing a PIL by the Just Rights for Children Alliance, the bench led by CJI Surya Kant with Justice Joymalya Bagchi asked the Centre to frame intermediary rules ensuring platforms admit only users aged 18+, noting minors cannot enter contracts under Section 11 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872; notices were issued to MeitY on 10 September.

capsules.title: SC declines early hearing in Bengal SIR roll-exclusion appeals
capsules.body: CJI Surya Kant’s bench refused to advance the hearing on appeals against West Bengal electoral-roll exclusions, saying ‘these are only by-elections’ ahead of the 6 October Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls; over 18,000 appeals are pending, and the ECI says 1,26,194 of 38,31,429 appeals were decided by 16 September.

capsules.title: SC wants WB Speaker to decide 10 MLAs’ disqualification pleas in 3 months
capsules.body: A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant disposed of Sohandeb Chattopadhyay’s petition expressing the desire that the West Bengal Speaker decide within three months the Tenth Schedule disqualification pleas against 10 MLAs of the Ritabrata Banerjee faction, filed on 8 July.

capsules.title: SC sets 3-month deadline for EC on TMC name dispute
capsules.body: On Mamata Banerjee’s Article 32 petition, the Supreme Court directed the warring faction to file its reply within four weeks and the Election Commission to decide the TMC name and symbol dispute within three months thereafter.

capsules.title: SC stays Delhi HC ruling upholding GST search of advocate's office
capsules.body: A bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu stayed the Delhi High Court judgment that had upheld the GST department's search of Advocate Puneet Batra's office and seizure of his computers under Section 67(2) of the CGST Act, 2017. The HC had held advocate-client privilege is no absolute bar where prima facie material suggests the lawyer acted beyond the adviser's role.

capsules.title: Sohrabuddin case: SC to examine acquittal of 22, not Shah's discharge
capsules.body: A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana agreed to examine the acquittal of 22 accused in the Sohrabuddin Shaikh encounter case but refused to revisit Amit Shah's discharge, declining to enter paragraph 43 of the Bombay High Court judgment.

capsules.title: 'Medical fraternity cannot be attacked': SC stays bail in doctors' assault case
capsules.body: Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta stayed the Bombay High Court order granting bail to a Shiv Sena corporator accused of assaulting doctors at a Kalyan municipal hospital, observing the message must go out that the medical fraternity cannot be touched, and directed surrender within three days.

capsules.title: Bareboat charter ends on valid termination notice: SC vacates vessel arrest
capsules.body: In Owners of M.V. Nereus Progress v. Om Freight Forwarders Ltd. (2026 INSC 1055), the Supreme Court set aside the Madras High Court and held a demise (bareboat) charter ends on a termination notice complying with contractual preconditions; physical repossession only completes the transfer, so the sister-vessel arrest could not stand.

capsules.title: SC dismisses Percept appeal against Rs 14.49-crore award to Ganguly
capsules.body: The Supreme Court refused to entertain Percept Talent Management's challenge to the Calcutta High Court judgment upholding a Rs 14.49-crore arbitral award to Sourav Ganguly under their 2003 Player Representation Agreement, reiterating the narrow scope of interference with arbitral awards.

capsules.title: Preventive detention cannot substitute bail cancellation: Karnataka HC
capsules.body: A Division Bench of Justices M. Nagaprasanna and Hema Kulkarni held preventive detention cannot be a convenient substitute for cancelling bail or a device to bypass a judicial order granting liberty. Ordering the immediate release of Raju Kale, detained under the Prevention of Illicit Traffic in Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act by a 3 July 2026 order, the Court found he was never informed of his right to make a representation to the Union government — a failure cutting at the root of the Article 22(5) safeguard.

capsules.title: Citizenship is the Home Ministry's job, not the ECI's: ex-SC judge Dhulia
capsules.body: Former Supreme Court judge Sudhanshu Dhulia (retired August 2025) said at the Indian Express Idea Exchange that the Supreme Court has laid down in several judgments that determining citizenship is the Ministry of Home Affairs' job, not the Election Commission's — though a voter must be a citizen. He called it 'a serious matter' that two Election Commissioners had objected on record 14 times in 10 months to steps by the Chief Election Commissioner.

capsules.title: Preventive detention cannot rest on bare assumption of bail: Bombay HC
capsules.body: Setting aside a detention order dated 6 December 2025, the Bombay High Court held the detaining authority's subjective satisfaction that the petitioner was likely to be released on bail rested on a bare assumption that the offence was not compulsorily punishable with death — not on cogent material — and the grounds of detention showed non-application of mind, affecting the petitioner's right to make the earliest effective representation. (Aman @ Aman Ibrahim Khan v. Commissioner of Police, Pune)

capsules.title: SC stays GST action on lawyer's seized data till 28 September
capsules.body: The Supreme Court directed that no coercive GST action be taken on data seized from a lawyer until 28 September 2026, protecting professional privilege and confidentiality of client information pending further hearing.

capsules.title: Bail cannot turn on a monetary settlement with the complainant: Delhi HC
capsules.body: The Delhi High Court held that bail cannot be granted or cancelled on the basis of fulfilment of a monetary settlement with the complainant, and that an undertrial's liberty cannot be made conditional on paying Rs 45 lakh under a settlement. Whether a settlement is enforceable between the parties is legally distinct from whether an undertrial may be deprived of liberty; the bail application must be reconsidered afresh on its own merits.

capsules.title: SC split verdict on sending Election Commissioner appointment case to larger bench
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, a two-judge bench delivered a split verdict on the Centre's demand to refer the Election Commissioner appointment case to a larger bench: Justice Dipankar Datta rejected the reference while Justice Satish Chandra Sharma accepted it.

capsules.title: SC urges CJI to constitute permanent 5-judge Constitution Bench
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Supreme Court urged the Chief Justice of India to constitute a permanent five-judge Constitution Bench to decide long-pending constitutional cases, flagging delays in adjudication of Constitution Bench matters.

capsules.title: SC orders re-induction of war widow Priyanka Saxena into IAF
capsules.body: A bench of CJI Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana directed the re-induction of former Short Service Commission officer Priyanka Saxena, widow of a fighter pilot killed in a 2021 MiG-21 crash. Exercising Article 142 powers, the Court called it a one-off order creating no precedent: she will undergo one-year refresher training and rejoin as Squadron Leader in her eleventh year of service, counting prior service.

capsules.title: Missing railway ticket cannot defeat compensation claim: SC
capsules.body: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar restored a Railway Claims Tribunal award of Rs 8 lakh with 9% interest to the parents of a passenger who fell from a train. Relying on Union of India v. Rina Devi (2018), the Court held the mere absence of a ticket does not negate bona fide travel — the claimant discharges the initial burden by affidavit and the onus shifts to the Railways. A delayed investigation report under the 2003 Rules was disregarded.

capsules.title: SC acquits rape accused, rejects trial court's 'value judgment'
capsules.body: Justices Ujjal Bhuyan and Atul S. Chandurkar acquitted Paramjit Singh Bedi, holding a court cannot partly reject a prosecutrix's testimony for a Section 366 IPC charge and accept the same statement for Section 376. The trial judge had 'gone completely wrong' in justifying conviction through personal value judgment; immorality without clinching evidence cannot sustain a conviction.

capsules.title: SC reserves verdict on pleas against Sambhal mosque survey
capsules.body: Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe reserved verdict on the Jama Masjid committee's challenge to the Allahabad High Court's 19 May 2025 order upholding a court-ordered survey in the Shahi Jama Masjid–Harihar temple dispute. Arguments invoked the Places of Worship (Special Provisions) Act, 1991 and the Supreme Court's 12 December 2024 restraint on fresh suits over religious places.

capsules.title: SC takes suo motu cognisance of Patna HC's 'offending' remarks
capsules.body: A three-judge bench of CJI Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana took suo motu cognisance (SMWP (Crl.) 5/2026) of a 9 July Patna High Court verdict holding that attempting to remove a woman's salwar and pressing her chest did not constitute attempt to rape. The bench called the observations 'offending' and directed notice to the accused, Himanshu Kumar Pathak, before deciding whether to set the judgment aside.

capsules.title: SC revises Noida DM order; NSA quashing stays
capsules.body: Justices Satish Chandra Sharma and N. Kotiswar Singh clarified that the Supreme Court had NOT stayed the Allahabad High Court's quashing of DU student Akriti Chaudhary's NSA detention — only the strictures against Gautam Buddha Nagar DM Medha Roopam and the Rs 5 lakh compensation from her salary were paused. The High Court had warned unchecked abuse of power risked an 'Orwellian dystopia'.

capsules.title: Seal residential premises used commercially; no pick-and-choose: SC
capsules.body: Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan directed municipal bodies nationwide to prioritise sealing premises in purely residential areas used for commercial activity, warning discriminatory 'pick-and-choose' enforcement would invite a strict view. The pan-India exercise grew from a Chennai illegal-construction plea expanded in March 2026; pendency of title litigation will not block sealing.

capsules.title: SC rejects plea to make Hindi its official language
capsules.body: A bench headed by CJI Surya Kant with Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana dismissed a plea seeking Hindi as the Supreme Court's official language. The Court held such language reforms cannot be introduced through judicial orders and need constitutional and legislative processes, noting gradual steps toward multilingual access to judgments are already underway.

capsules.title: Fair investigation is an Article 21 right: SC orders de novo SIT probe
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Supreme Court ordered an SIT de novo probe into the 2012 Dharmasthala minor's rape-murder, rejecting 'golden hour' reasoning and holding that a fair investigation is a constitutional right under Article 21.

capsules.title: Collegium recommends 12 additional judges be made permanent in four High Courts
capsules.body: The Supreme Court Collegium — CJI Surya Kant with Justices Vikram Nath and B.V. Nagarathna — approved the proposal to appoint 12 additional judges as permanent judges: five in Andhra Pradesh, five in Kerala, and one each in Uttarakhand (Justice Subhash Upadhyay) and Gauhati (Justice Kaushik Goswami).

capsules.title: Jagadhri acquisition upheld but compensation at 2026 rates: P&H HC
capsules.body: A Division Bench of Justices Vikas Bahl and Divya Sharma upheld a 25-year-old acquisition for a Jagadhri road but ordered compensation at the Collector's rate on the judgment date (14 September 2026) under the 2013 Act, with 100% solatium and 12% interest under Section 30(3). Dispensing with Section 5-A objections under the 1894 Act without application of mind was faulted, but quashing was refused in public interest.

capsules.title: Calcutta HC quashes EPFO's pro-rata method for higher pension
capsules.body: The Calcutta High Court struck down the EPFO's 14 February 2024 circular mandating pro-rata computation of higher pension — the third High Court to reject the method after Himachal Pradesh and Punjab & Haryana. Higher pension must rest on the average salary of the last 60 months of service, not an artificial pre/post-September 2014 split.

capsules.title: Review Medical Board is not a matter of right: Karnataka HC
capsules.body: Justice C.M. Poonacha dismissed Army aspirant Monish N. Aradhya's plea for a Review Medical Board after he was found medically unfit over a small left kidney despite ranking 51st in merit. Under the Manual of Medical Standards, a kidney under 8 cm on ultrasound means rejection, and the AMB's triple-phase CECT scan (7 cm) was more accurate than private ultrasounds.

capsules.title: Delhi HC grants bail to Jagtar Singh Johal in seven NIA cases
capsules.body: Justices Navin Chawla and Ravinder Dudeja granted bail to British national Jagtar Singh Johal, jailed since November 2017, citing prolonged incarceration of over eight years, a sluggish trial (only 40 of 123 witnesses examined) and his March 2025 acquittal in one case as of 'strong persuasive value'. Conditions include surrendering his passport and staying off social-media groups circulating anti-national material.

capsules.title: Telangana HC disqualifies Danam Nagender under Tenth Schedule
capsules.body: A Division Bench of Chief Justice Aparesh Kumar Singh and Justice G.M. Mohiuddin disqualified Khairatabad MLA Danam Nagender with effect from 23 April 2024 under paragraph 2(1)(a) of the Tenth Schedule, setting aside the Speaker's order. Contesting the 2024 Lok Sabha poll on a Congress ticket after winning the Assembly seat on a BRS ticket amounted to voluntarily giving up party membership.

capsules.title: Delhi HC notifies new Senior Advocate designation rules
capsules.body: The Delhi High Court notified amended designation rules scrapping the 100-point evaluation by a permanent committee. Designation will now be by the full court through consensus or a two-thirds majority vote, with a permanent secretariat headed by a registrar-rank officer compiling candidate data annually — following the Supreme Court's May 2025 reading down of the points system.

capsules.title: Punjab must acquire Army officer's land held since 1972: P&H HC
capsules.body: The Punjab and Haryana High Court directed Punjab to acquire 10.5 marlas of a retired Army officer's land under unauthorised state occupation since 1972, when the PWD built a road on it. The state must issue the Section 11 notification under the 2013 Act forthwith, complete acquisition in three months, and pay 6% simple interest on the award amount from 1972 (the start of the unauthorised occupation).

capsules.title: State can't invoke 3-month deadline after wrongly rejecting pleas: Telangana HC
capsules.body: A Division Bench of Justices P. Sam Koshy and Vakiti Ramakrishna Reddy held the three-month deadline under Section 28-A of the Land Acquisition Act cannot defeat landowners whose timely Section 18 applications for a compensation reference were wrongly rejected. Dismissing the state's appeal, the Court protected re-determination claims anchored to a court's enhanced award.

capsules.title: Karnataka HC restores DRDO land acquisition quashed by single judge
capsules.body: A bench of Justices D.K. Singh and H. Shanthi Bhushan allowed the Union of India's writ appeals and restored acquisition of about 1.5 acres at Benniganahalli village, Bengaluru East, adjoining DRDO's Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics. The Court held a defence laboratory cannot be built around plots left out of it.

capsules.title: ECI: later SIR decisions unanimous; only original order upheld by Supreme Court
capsules.body: The Election Commission stated that Special Intensive Revision decisions taken after the original order had the unanimous approval of all three Election Commissioners; only the original 24 June 2025 order was upheld by the Supreme Court on 27 May 2026. SIR stands completed in 20 States/UTs including Bihar and West Bengal, with final elector figures due after Phase-III publication in the remaining 12 States; changes to Form 6 were also upheld.

capsules.title: Film copyright licensing GST is 12%, not 18%: Bombay HC
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Bombay High Court held GST on a producer's licensing of film copyrights is 12% and set aside a Rs 12.11-crore demand against Dharma Productions.

capsules.title: EU sanctions can't override Indian-law contract: Delhi HC
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Delhi High Court granted interim relief under Order XXXIX Rules 1–2 CPC directing SAP India to restore support services to Nayara Energy, holding EU sanctions cannot override a contract governed by Indian law; the main suit remains pending.

capsules.title: Rehabilitation claims can't survive IBC clean slate: MP HC
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Madhya Pradesh High Court held project-affected persons' rehabilitation claims cannot survive the IBC's clean-slate doctrine against a successful resolution applicant.

capsules.title: MP HC affirms direction to reframe daily-rated staff regularisation policy
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Madhya Pradesh High Court affirmed a direction to the state to reframe its regularisation policy for daily-rated employees.

capsules.title: GST arrest after court-monitored cooperation is Article 21 violation: P&H HC
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Punjab and Haryana High Court pulled up the GST department for converting a court-monitored cooperation exercise into an arrest operation, calling it a 'brazen violation of Article 21'.

capsules.title: Allahabad HC acquits mother on death row over tutored child witness
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Allahabad High Court acquitted a mother on death row for murdering her three sons, citing a tutored child witness and investigative lapses.

capsules.title: TIP not fatal where identity otherwise proved: Madras HC
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Madras High Court held non-conduct of a test identification parade is not fatal where the accused's identity is otherwise established, upholding life sentences in an acid-attack case.

capsules.title: Delhi HC restores PwBD reservation at MBBS stage; UDID card is key document
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Delhi High Court restored reservation for persons with benchmark disabilities at the MBBS admission stage, holding the disability percentage on the UDID card to be binding, while the NMC medical board assesses the candidate's functional ability for the course.

capsules.title: SC notifies December 2026 Advocate-on-Record examination dates
capsules.body: Reported during 21–27 September 2026, the Supreme Court notified the schedule for the December 2026 Advocate-on-Record examination: 19, 20, 22 and 23 December 2026, for qualifying re-appearance candidates.

capsules.title: Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act 2026 comes into force
capsules.body: By gazette notification, the Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment) Act, 2026 (12 of 2026) comes into force on 1 October 2026. Delayed registration between one and two years needs a DM, SDM or executive magistrate's order; beyond two years needs a Judicial Magistrate First Class order — tightening the 1969 Act's Section 13(3) to encourage timely reporting.

capsules.title: SC quashes Mulla Afroz's NSA detention; Rs 10 lakh costs on UP
capsules.body: On 29 September 2026 the Supreme Court quashed Mulla Afroz's NSA preventive detention in the Sambhal case, set aside the Allahabad High Court ruling and imposed Rs 10 lakh costs on Uttar Pradesh.

capsules.title: Ratio: custodial confession alone cannot ground NSA detention
capsules.body: The Supreme Court held that a custodial confession by itself cannot support a preventive detention order under the NSA - the authority must have independent material.

capsules.title: Article 142: mutual-consent divorce despite Section 13B waiting-period issues
capsules.body: The Supreme Court held it can invoke Article 142 to dissolve a marriage by mutual consent where there is a complete settlement, even if the Section 13B waiting period faces procedural issues.

capsules.title: SC refuses interim stay on UPI MDR proposal
capsules.body: The Supreme Court declined interim relief against the proposed MDR on specified UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000; the Centre, RBI and NPCI must respond in four weeks.

capsules.title: Article 22(5): grounds must be communicated to the detenu
capsules.body: Preventive detention requires the authority to communicate the grounds of detention and give the detenu the earliest opportunity to make a representation - the safeguard at the heart of the Mulla Afroz ruling.

capsules.title: NSA detention capped at 12 months
capsules.body: Section 13 of the National Security Act, 1980 caps preventive detention at twelve months from the date of detention.

capsules.title: Bihar vigilance raids: Rs 1.07 cr disproportionate-assets case under PCA + BNS 61(2)
capsules.body: The Bihar Vigilance Investigation Bureau searched four premises of Patna ADM (Supply) Ravindra Kumar Diwakar and his wife, Danapur Sub-Registrar Kumari Sweety, on 30 September 2026, recovering nearly Rs 80 lakh cash, Rs 52.6 lakh jewellery and 48 watches in a Rs 1.07 crore disproportionate-assets case registered 25 September under the Prevention of Corruption Act and BNS Section 61(2).

capsules.title: UPI MDR 0.4% above Rs 2,000 from 15 October; SC asks Centre to explain
capsules.body: The Supreme Court on 30 September asked the Centre to explain the 0.4% MDR framework on selected UPI merchant transactions above Rs 2,000 — effective 15 October 2026 — while declining an interim stay; NPCI chief Dilip Asbe said about 75% of merchants will face no additional cost.

capsules.title: INDIA bloc readies CEC removal motion; march to EC on 6 October
capsules.body: At its 30 September meeting, the INDIA bloc announced a march to the Election Commission office on 6 October and readied a draft motion for the removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged voter-list manipulation.

capsules.title: ECI relaxes Form 6 declaration rule in non-SIR states
capsules.body: The Election Commission on 30 September reverted to allowing online Form 6 submission — used for fresh voter registration under the Representation of the People Act, 1950 — without the attached declaration in states where the SIR of electoral rolls is not underway.

capsules.title: SEBI overhauls portfolio management and settlement rules
capsules.body: SEBI's board on 30 September 2026 cleared a sweeping overhaul of portfolio management and settlement rules — key securities-law framework for CLAT/AILET legal GK.

capsules.title: SC: courts must not impose personal views on morality in criminal cases
capsules.body: The Supreme Court on 1 October 2026 held that courts must refrain from imposing their personal views on morality while deciding criminal cases — a key jurisprudence holding for CLAT/AILET legal reasoning.

capsules.title: ECI removes SIR declaration from Form 6 in finalised states
capsules.body: The Election Commission removed the Special Intensive Revision declaration from the statutory voter enrolment form (Form 6) in states where the revision has been finalised, following its 30 September relaxation in non-SIR states.

capsules.title: Centre cuts windfall tax on diesel and ATF exports
capsules.body: The government cut the windfall tax on diesel and aviation turbine fuel exports, a tax-policy development with indirect-tax law implications.

capsules.title: BJD plans marches from 2 October against amended Odisha mining law
capsules.body: The BJD planned marches across Odisha from 2 October against the amended mining law, after a bandh over errors in school textbooks saw a partial response — state legislation and protest law in the news.

capsules.title: AITA to hold fresh elections on 27 November after court-directed overhaul
capsules.body: The All India Tennis Association announced fresh elections for 27 November following a court-directed overhaul — sports-governance litigation in current legal GK.

capsules.title: CLAT 2027: 6 December 2026; apply by 31 October
capsules.body: CLAT 2027 will be held on 6 December 2026 (2–4 PM); the Consortium of NLUs opened applications on 3 August 2026 and the last date is 31 October 2026. Fee: Rs 4,000 (General/OBC/NRI/PIO/OCI) and Rs 3,500 (SC/ST/BPL/PwD).

capsules.title: 'Child Marriage-Free Village' resolution: legal angle
capsules.body: The WCD Ministry directed all gram panchayats to pass 'Child Marriage-Free Village' resolutions at the 2 October gram sabhas under the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Abhiyan; child marriage is prohibited under the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006, with certification by the Child Marriage Prohibition Officer.

capsules.title: Special gram sabhas: the 73rd Amendment in action
capsules.body: Special gram sabhas held nationwide on 2 October 2026 launched the People's Plan Campaign 2026-27 ('Sabki Yojana, Sabka Vikas'); the Gram Sabha is defined in Article 243A and is the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system created by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.

capsules.title: Special Campaign 6.0: e-waste rules in focus
capsules.body: Special Campaign 6.0 (2–31 October 2026) gives special emphasis to the scientific collection, segregation and disposal of e-waste; India regulates e-waste under the E-Waste (Management) Rules, 2022 (in force 1 April 2023) based on Extended Producer Responsibility.

capsules.title: Reform Utsav: reforms as a governance narrative
capsules.body: The 'Reform Utsav' campaign launched on 2 October 2026 by PM Modi celebrates transformative reforms across ministries, marking 12 years of transformative governance; the recent legal reforms — the three new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA, 2024) — sit within this narrative.

capsules.title: Karnataka: 2% sports quota in govt jobs
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Karnataka notified 2% reservation for sportspersons in government jobs, with weightage marks for national and international achievements; unfilled quota posts revert to the same category's vertical reservation.

capsules.title: BoB pension fund: PFRDA S.27 nod
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — Bank of Baroda received PFRDA's Certificate of Appointment as Sponsor of a pension fund under Section 27 of the PFRDA Act, 2013, becoming the second public sector bank in the pension fund business after SBI (April 2008).

capsules.title: India–Switzerland pacts signed
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — India and Switzerland signed pacts on migration, young professionals, transport and research & innovation as PM Modi met Swiss President Guy Parmelin, agreeing to deepen cooperation in defence production and nuclear energy.

capsules.title: CRPF sports quota: eligibility window
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — CRPF's 521-post sports-quota recruitment (182 Head Constable GD + 339 Constable GD) requires sports achievements/certificates of the last two years; applications run 12 Oct–11 Nov 2026 at rect.crpf.gov.in.

capsules.title: eSanjeevani: 50 crore consultations
capsules.body: 8 Oct 2026 — The Health Ministry reported that eSanjeevani, India's national telemedicine platform, crossed 50 crore online medical consultations on 15 September 2026.

capsules.title: GST decriminalisation: the 57th Council's legal pivot
capsules.body: The 57th GST Council (8 October 2026) recommended removing GST officers' power to arrest taxpayers, raising the prosecution threshold from Rs 1 crore to Rs 5 crore, removing the minimum punishment for GST offences and halving the general penalty to Rs 10,000 — a textbook decriminalisation-and-due-process case study for CLAT legal reasoning.

capsules.title: JOSH and public-health law
capsules.body: JOSH (Joint Squad for Health) teams launched 8 October 2026 under the TB Mukt Bharat Abhiyan join three ministries for grassroots TB case-finding; note the State's public-health powers and the volunteer-mobilisation model for polity/health-law questions.

capsules.title: India–Ghana: two MoUs
capsules.body: India and Ghana exchanged two MoUs on scientific research, academics, capacity building, agricultural research and education during the EAM's West Africa visit — revise treaty-making practice and international agreements for the legal-affairs section.

capsules.title: 153rd IPU Assembly: parliamentary diplomacy
capsules.body: An Indian parliamentary delegation led by Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh departed for the 153rd Inter-Parliamentary Union Assembly in Arusha, Tanzania — useful context for questions on parliamentary institutions.

capsules.title: Uttarakhand: sixth fully literate state
capsules.body: Uttarakhand's declaration as India's sixth fully literate state (6 October 2026) under NEP 2020 and the ULLAS programme ties directly to the right to education (Article 21A) and the RTE Act, 2009.

capsules.subject: Legal GK
capsules.title: US sanctions the ICC — international law under pressure (9 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Hours after the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize went to Navi Pillay, the United States announced sanctions on the International Criminal Court on 9 October 2026 — cutting it off from US companies and financial services, with a six-month wind-down waiver. The ICC condemned the move as an 'assault on the rule of law and the very foundations of the international legal order'. Foreign ministers of Canada, Denmark, Germany, France, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands and the UK jointly reaffirmed 'continued and unwavering support' for the court.

capsules.subject: Constitutional law
capsules.title: Jantar Mantar denotified as Delhi's protest site (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Following recommendations of a committee constituted by the Union Home Ministry, Delhi Police removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest sites in October 2026 and designated three alternative venues: Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground (East Delhi). The Delhi High Court is to hear a plea challenging the move on 13 October 2026. The development follows the October protests demanding the Election Commission's accountability.

capsules.subject: Constitutional law
capsules.title: Kerala Assembly resolution seeks removal of CEC (Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Kerala Assembly passed a resolution in October 2026 seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The resolution also demanded that the panel selecting election commissioners include the Prime Minister, the Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition and the Chief Justice of India.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: SC on Form 6: ‘no adjudication’; petitions on 27 October (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: On 12 October 2026, the Supreme Court (bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V. Mohana) clarified it had “neither approved nor disapproved” the Election Commission’s revised Form 6 for voter registration. The bench said its May 27, 2026 judgment (Association for Democratic Reforms v. ECI, 2026 INSC 564) upheld the Bihar SIR’s legality but pre-dated the July 2026 form changes (ancestry/roll-linkage declarations on ECINet). Rejecting the ECI’s claim of judicial approval — “Do not put words in our mouth” — the Court observed there had been no adjudication on the new form and posted the challenges (including petitioner Priya Mishra’s) for 27 October 2026.

capsules.subject: Family Law
capsules.title: SC: limited estate can ripen into absolute ownership under Section 14(1) HSA (9 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: In a judgment dated 9 October 2026, the Supreme Court dismissed a civil appeal and held that a Hindu woman’s qualifying limited estate can become absolute ownership under Section 14(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, clarifying the provision’s interaction with the Delhi Land Reforms Act, 1954 in the succession to agricultural land. The Division Bench judgment sustaining the respondents’ mutation claim was left undisturbed. Key exam takeaway: Section 14(1) converts a woman’s limited interest into full ownership where the statutory conditions are met, overriding restrictive succession routes under land-reform statutes in the circumstances considered.

capsules.subject: Criminal Law
capsules.title: Punjab CBI case: SC bars coercive action, FIR stays (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: On 12 October 2026, a Supreme Court bench of Justices M.M. Sundresh and Prasanna B. Varale directed the CBI not to take coercive steps in the corruption case involving officials linked to Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann’s office — but refused to stay the FIR, so the investigation continues. The case arose after an ED communication to Punjab’s DGP alleging influence over transfers, postings, tenders and policy decisions; the Punjab and Haryana High Court had on 5 October 2026 directed the CBI to register a case and report within two months. Punjab’s challenge to that order is pending; the interim order is not a finding of guilt.

capsules.subject: Constitutional law
capsules.title: SC notice on PIL against immunity to CEC, ECs (13 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: On 13 October 2026, the Supreme Court issued notice to the Centre and the Election Commission of India on a public interest litigation challenging the blanket immunity granted to the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners under Section 16 of the Chief Election Commissioner and other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.

capsules.subject: International law
capsules.title: IBCA headquarters inaugurated (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The International Big Cat Alliance headquarters at 55 Lodhi Estate, New Delhi, was inaugurated on 12 October 2026 by Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav. A treaty-based intergovernmental body covering tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma, it was approved by the Union Cabinet on 29 February 2024 with Rs 150 crore over five years and has 29 member countries including India.

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls challenged in the Supreme Court
capsules.body: In October 2026 AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi moved the Supreme Court challenging the manner in which the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls is being conducted; the Court agreed to hear the plea along with other pending petitions. Separately, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi and 10 opposition leaders moved the top court against alleged malpractices in the SIR process.

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: Supreme Court Senior Personal Assistant Recruitment 2026: 65 posts
capsules.body: The Supreme Court Registry released Advt No. F.6/11/SPA/2026-SC (RC) for direct recruitment of 65 Senior Personal Assistants (Group B, Non-Gazetted). Graduates with English shorthand at 110 w.p.m. and computer typing at 40 w.p.m. can apply online at sci.gov.in from 20 October to 10 November 2026. Pay: Level 8 (₹47,600–₹1,51,100); selection through objective test, shorthand test, typing test and interview.

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: Supreme Court Court Master (Shorthand): 15 deputation posts
capsules.body: The Supreme Court notified 15 Court Master (Shorthand) posts on deputation (Notification No. F.6(CM(S))/2026-SC(RC), dated 12 October 2026) for serving stenographic personnel of High Courts and District Courts. Pay: Level 11 (₹67,700–₹2,08,700); eligibility includes a degree, English shorthand at 120 w.p.m., typing at 40 w.p.m., and age not exceeding 56 years.

capsules.subject: International Law
capsules.title: 2026 Nobel Peace Prize: Navi Pillay and international justice
capsules.body: South African jurist Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay received the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law, including accountability for war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide across global judicial bodies. She earlier served as a judge of the International Criminal Court and as UN High Commissioner for Human Rights.

capsules.subject: CLAT
capsules.title: CLAT 2027: applications close 31 October 2026
capsules.body: Applications for the CLAT 2027 cycle (Consortium of NLUs) opened 3 August 2026 and close on 31 October 2026 at consortiumofnlus.ac.in; the exam is on 6 December 2026. Fee: Rs 4,000 (Gen/OBC), Rs 3,500 (SC/ST). UG eligibility: 10+2 with 45% (40% for reserved categories); PG: LLB with 55% (50% for reserved).

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: Meerut 'Blue Drum' murder case: death sentence
capsules.body: A Meerut court sentenced Muskan Rastogi and Sahil Shukla to death for the murder of Saurabh Rajput in the widely reported 'Blue Drum' murder case (Oct 2026).

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: SC: conversion does not automatically grant backward-class reservation (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: A Bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar held on 15 October 2026 that a member of a backward Hindu community does not automatically become a member of a notified backward Muslim community merely by converting to Islam. The Court dismissed the Tamil Nadu government's appeal against a Madras High Court order that struck down the State's 9 March 2024 order (an 'artificial group' entitled to reservation), and referred to the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, which restricts SC recognition to persons professing Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism. The case arose from Sameer Ahamed, who converted from Hinduism to Islam in 2015.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: SC upholds quashing of Yes Bank's ₹8,415 crore AT1 bond write-off (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: A Bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih held on 15 October 2026 — 'we see no reason to interfere with the impugned judgment' — upholding the Bombay High Court's 20 January 2023 judgment that quashed Yes Bank's write-down of AT1 bonds worth ₹8,415 crore in its March 2020 restructuring (Yes Bank v Axis Trusteeship). The RBI had placed Yes Bank under moratorium on 5 March 2020 and framed a reconstruction scheme under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; the administrator announced the bond write-off on 14 March 2020, challenged by Axis Trustee Services on behalf of debenture holders.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: SC: mandatory insurance on all offline railway tickets from 27 Oct 2026
capsules.body: A Bench of Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah and R. Mahadevan directed on 15 October 2026 that tickets sold at counters at every railway station nationwide must include travel insurance coverage identical to that of online bookings, with the order to take effect from 27 October 2026 — a public-interest expansion of consumer protection for rail passengers.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: CJI: SC to decide on plea to recall CEC law order; SIR scrutiny (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: CJI Surya Kant said on 15 October 2026 that the Supreme Court will soon decide on the plea to recall the CEC law order. In the same sitting's related developments, the Court agreed to examine the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of Delhi's electoral rolls (petition by Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders filed 12 October 2026 seeking an independent audit of voter-database changes), the validity of revised Form 6, and the government's de-notification of Jantar Mantar as a protest site.

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: SC roundup: NEET-PG answer-key plea, Rajpal Yadav passport, Bar Council letter on judges (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Supreme Court (15 Oct 2026) sought the Centre's response on NEET-PG 2026 answer-key transparency, and in the Rajpal Yadav cheque-bounce case allowed release of his passport for work travel. Separately, the Bar Council of Delhi wrote to CJI Surya Kant condemning personal attacks on judges. (Dated: 16 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: SC: zero tolerance for AI-hallucinated precedents (14 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Supreme Court set aside tribunal orders that relied on AI-generated 'hallucinated' case law, holding that a decision using fake material 'is no decision at all' and amounts to subversion of the rule of law. It directed the Bar Council of India to constitute a committee on guiding principles and disciplinary consequences for advocates submitting fake precedents. This followed its draft Regulations for Use of AI in Courts, 2026.

capsules.subject: Banking law
capsules.title: Yes Bank AT-1 bonds: SC dismisses appeals (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih dismissed appeals in Yes Bank Ltd. & Anr. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd. & Ors. (2026 INSC 1132), leaving the Bombay High Court's 20 January 2023 decision — which set aside the Rs. 8,415 crore AT-1 bond write-down — undisturbed, under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

capsules.subject: CLAT
capsules.title: CLAT 2027: no syllabus or pattern change; expert-panel reforms deferred — Verified: 17 Oct 2026
capsules.body: The Consortium of National Law Universities notified CLAT 2027 on 22 July 2026: registration ran 3 August–31 October 2026 and the exam is on 6 December 2026 (2:00–4:00 PM, offline pen-and-paper). The paper retains 120 MCQs across five sections with 0.25 negative marking, and the Governing Body confirmed no change to syllabus or sections. Recommendations of the CLAT Expert Committee Report will be considered for CLAT 2028 onward, with a committee to be constituted by the CJI's office.

capsules.subject: Legal reasoning
capsules.title: CLAT 2027: exam 6 Dec; registration closes 31 Oct
capsules.body: The Consortium of National Law Universities is accepting CLAT 2027 applications till 31 October 2026 (11:59 PM) at consortiumofnlus.ac.in (registration opened 3 August 2026). The offline exam is on Sunday, 6 December 2026, 2–4 PM (PwD candidates till 4:40 PM): 120 questions, 120 marks, 2 hours, minus 0.25 per wrong answer across five sections, for admission to 26 participating NLUs. Fee: ₹4,000 (General/OBC/PwD/NRI), ₹3,500 (SC/ST/BPL). There is no change in syllabus or pattern this year (Consortium notification 22 July 2026); about 92,000 candidates are expected for roughly 4,092 UG and 1,599 PG seats. Admit card is expected in the third week of November; result around the third week of December 2026.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: CLAT 2027 eligibility: 45% (Gen/OBC), 40% (SC/ST), no age limit
capsules.body: CLAT 2027 eligibility (Consortium notification 22 July 2026): UG — 45% in Class 12 for General/OBC, 40% for SC/ST; students appearing in Class 12 in 2027 may apply; no upper age limit. PG — LL.B. with 50% (45% for SC/ST/PwD). Applications are accepted only through the official Consortium portal; counselling is expected in December 2026/January 2027.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: Internet access is a fundamental right — for children too
capsules.body: 17 October 2026 — A Supreme Court Bench of Justices J. B. Pardiwala and K. Vinod Chandran held the right to access and use the internet a fundamental right of every individual under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a), expressly extending it to children: denying them internet altogether in the name of safety would be unreasonable, since safety and freedom are not at odds. The ruling came while directing stronger mechanisms against child sexual exploitation material online.

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: Yes Bank AT-1: 2026 INSC 1132 sets aside write-down
capsules.body: 15 October 2026 — In Yes Bank Ltd. v. Axis Trustee Services Ltd. (2026 INSC 1132), the Supreme Court dismissed appeals by Yes Bank, the RBI and the Union of India against the Bombay High Court's order setting aside the write-down of AT-1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore. Central principle: administrative action in bank reconstruction must remain within the authority of the statute, the RBI's Basel III framework and the final Reconstruction Scheme. Bench: Justices Dipankar Datta and Augustine George Masih.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: False election affidavits: private complaints allowed
capsules.body: 16 October 2026 — The Supreme Court held that private citizens may file criminal complaints against candidates who furnish false information in election affidavits under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951, and that Section 195 CrPC is no bar. Bench: Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: Temple land cannot be gifted to the State
capsules.body: 17 October 2026 — The Supreme Court ruled the government is only a custodian of temple properties and cannot accept temple land as a gift even for public use. It declared illegal a 2017 gift deed transferring land of the Nagapalayam Mariamman-Ponnachiamman Temple (Erode) for a Taluk Office, holding it violated the TN Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Act, 1959, and ordered Rs 31,000 monthly rent. Bench: Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe.

capsules.subject: Constitution
capsules.title: Conversion does not carry backward-class status
capsules.body: 15 October 2026 — Upholding the Madras High Court, the Supreme Court held that a person converting from Hinduism to Islam cannot claim Backward Class Muslim reservation on pre-conversion caste status, striking down a 2024 Tamil Nadu government order. Affirmative action under Article 16(4) cannot rest on the social backwardness of a pre-conversion identity. Bench: Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar.

capsules.subject: Judiciary
capsules.title: Direct recruits rank above compassionate appointees
capsules.body: 9 October 2026 (M. Prema v. State of Tamil Nadu, 2026 INSC 1105) — The Supreme Court held that direct recruits selected through the regular process cannot be placed below compassionate appointees in seniority merely because the latter joined earlier. Compassionate appointment is an exception to normal recruitment and confers no preferential right to seniority — reaffirming equality in public employment.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: CLAT 2027: registration closes 31 October; exam on 6 December
capsules.body: The Consortium of National Law Universities will close CLAT 2027 applications at 11:59 PM on 31 October 2026 at consortiumofnlus.ac.in; incomplete forms will not be considered and no edits are allowed after the closing date. The offline test for the 2027-28 academic session is scheduled for Sunday, 6 December 2026, from 2 PM to 4 PM (until 4:40 PM for PwD candidates). About 92,000 candidates are expected to compete for roughly 4,092 UG seats and 1,599 PG seats across 26 participating NLUs and IIULER Goa.

capsules.subject: Current Affairs
capsules.title: CLAT 2027 eligibility and fee structure
capsules.body: For the CLAT 2027 undergraduate programme, candidates need Class 12 with 45% marks (40% for SC/ST/PwD); those writing Class 12 boards in March-April 2027 can apply now. For the postgraduate programme, an LLB from a Bar Council of India-recognised university with 50% (45% for SC/ST) is required. There is no upper age limit. The application fee is Rs 4,000 for General/OBC and Rs 3,500 for SC/ST/BPL/PwD candidates. Foreign nationals cannot take CLAT and must apply to NLUs directly.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: SC: public bodies may scrap auctions to maximise price (16 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: In Satinder Pal Singh & Ors. v. Bedi Hospital & Ors. (16 October 2026; Bench: Justices P. S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe), the Supreme Court held that public authorities can call off an auction of government property and order a fresh sale if the move secures a higher price and maximises public revenue - such a decision is neither arbitrary nor unreasonable when guided by public interest and transparency. Under the Chandigarh Estate Rules, 2007, a binding contract is completed only after the allotment letter is issued and the conveyance deed executed; until then the administration retains the power to withdraw the property. The Court noted Bedi Hospital's Rs 12.58 crore winning bid for a nursing-home site was cancelled after an adjacent same-size plot fetched Rs 18.25 crore the same day, and directed a fresh e-auction within three months. - Verified: 20 Oct 2026

capsules.subject: Constitutional & Electoral Law
capsules.title: SC (16 Oct 2026): private complaints maintainable under Section 125A RPA for false election affidavits
capsules.body: In a judgment pronounced on 16 October 2026, a Supreme Court bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu held that private individuals can file criminal complaints against elected candidates for offences under Section 125A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 (knowingly furnishing false information or concealing material facts in nomination papers/election affidavits) — without the complaint of a public servant that Section 195(1) of the CrPC, 1973 requires for certain specified offences. Reasoning: Section 195(1) does not list Section 125A — 125A was inserted in 2002 while Section 195 was amended in 2006, and Parliament's omission was deliberate; Section 125A applies 'notwithstanding anything contained in any other law'; and Election Commission guidelines and press notes cannot determine statutory interpretation — that remains a judicial function. While settling the law, the Court upheld the Karnataka High Court's quashing of the specific proceedings — the complaint by Rajkumar Madki against Karnataka MLA Shailendra Beldale (Bidar) over an alleged false address declaration in his 2023 assembly-poll affidavit stood rebutted on record — adding that magistrates are equipped to deal with frivolous complaints intended to harass elected candidates. This expands voter-led enforcement of the disclosure obligation flowing from the ADR v. Union of India jurisprudence.

capsules.subject: Labour & Service Law
capsules.title: SC (6 Oct 2026): regularised daily-wage workers entitled to post-retirement annual increment
capsules.body: The Supreme Court held on 6 October 2026 (Chhaganbhai Kohyabhai Pateliya & Ors. v. State of Gujarat & Ors., 2026 LiveLaw (SC) 1020) that daily-wage skilled workers who were treated as permanent employees under a government resolution — and granted regular pay scales and retirement benefits — cannot be denied the annual increment falling due after their retirement merely because they were originally engaged as daily wagers. A bench of Justice Sanjay Kumar and Justice Sanjeev Sachdeva set aside the Gujarat High Court's division-bench judgment, relying on the 1988 state government resolution under which daily-wage skilled workers completing ten years' prescribed service were treated as permanent employees with regular pay scales, allowances, pension and other retiral benefits.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: Three new SC judges sworn in (6 Oct 2026); working strength 37, sanctioned 38
capsules.body: Three judges were sworn into the Supreme Court on 6 October 2026 by CJI Surya Kant — Justices Sunita Agarwal (formerly Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court), Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya (formerly Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court) and Aparesh Kumar Singh (formerly Chief Justice of the Telangana High Court) — taking the Court's working strength to 37 against a sanctioned strength of 38 (including the CJI), one vacancy. The sanctioned strength was raised from 34 to 38 by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026 (Rajya Sabha passed it on 5 August 2026; it replaced a May 2026 Ordinance). The women judges on the Court now number three. Key exam points: the number of SC judges is fixed by Parliament by law under Article 124(1) — not by constitutional amendment; oath under Article 124(6) read with the Third Schedule; retirement age 65; collegium jurisprudence from the Second (1993) and Third (1998) Judges cases.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: SC (9 Oct 2026): restrictions on protest must be proportionate — 'can't shut down an entire city'
capsules.body: On 9 October 2026, a three-judge Supreme Court bench headed by Chief Justice Surya Kant held that restrictions on protest must be proportionate, remarking that authorities 'can't shut down an entire city'. The writ petition followed the cancellation of train services to Delhi and the stopping of people in several States ahead of a demonstration planned for 10 October. The Court suggested an alternative open space for the rally, which the government agreed to. The ruling grounds the right in Article 19(1)(b) — the right to assemble peaceably and without arms — with any restriction required to be reasonable.

capsules.subject: Legal Education
capsules.title: SC reserves verdict on mandatory attendance rules for law students (7 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: On 7 October 2026, a Supreme Court bench of Justices Vikram Nath, Augustine George Masih and Sandeep Mehta reserved its judgment on petitions challenging the Delhi High Court's ruling that law students cannot be barred from examinations or academic progression solely for attendance shortages. The Bar Council of India (BCI) and leading law schools argued that diluting mandatory attendance norms degrades academic discipline, institutional autonomy and professional standards in legal education. The controversy stems from a suo motu PIL by the Delhi High Court following the 2016 suicide of Amity Law School student Sushant Rohilla, who faced repeating the year over poor attendance.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: SC: 30-day deadline to digitise all police stations; FIRs on CCTNS (21 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
21 Oct 2026 — S. Ganesh vs State of Tamil Nadu: The Supreme Court (Justices Ahsanuddin Amanullah & R. Mahadevan) held police stations without computers/internet “absolutely unacceptable” and gave states/UTs one month to provide basic digitisation hardware + internet (dedicated line or dongles).

Every FIR must be uploaded locally and transmitted to the state portal and national CCTNS; Child Welfare Committees must be fully digitised too. The case arose from a father's plea about his daughter missing from Chennai since 2011.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: Internet access is a fundamental right — for children too (SC, 15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
15 Oct 2026 — Just Rights for Children Alliance v. S. Harish (2026 INSC 1149): Justices J.B. Pardiwala & K. Vinod Chandran held internet access a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Article 19(1)(a), extending to children — blanket denial in the name of safety is unreasonable; safety and freedom “are not at odds.”

Context: directions to strengthen detection/removal of child sexual exploitation and abuse material (CSEAM) from social media and online services; Article 19(1)(a) includes the right to receive and impart information.

capsules.subject: Constitutional Law
capsules.title: Converts cannot claim pre-conversion backward-class status: SC (15 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
15 Oct 2026: The Supreme Court (Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra & Shree Chandrashekhar) upheld the Madras HC ruling that conversion from Hinduism to Islam does not automatically confer Backward Class Muslim status — pre-conversion caste cannot be transferred.

“A person who converts from the Hindu social order to a non-Hindu social order cannot claim affirmative action under Article 16(4) merely on the basis of the social backwardness associated with his pre-conversion status.” TN's 2024 GO on community certificates for converts was struck down.

capsules.subject: Media Law
capsules.title: MIB: AI only in assistive role in TV news; follow Programme Code (21 Oct 2026)
capsules.body:
21 Oct 2026 — MIB advisory: The Ministry of Information & Broadcasting advised private satellite TV channels to use AI only in an assistive capacity in news broadcasts — without compromising accuracy, authenticity or sensitivity — and to comply with the Programme Code under the Cable Television Networks (Regulation) Act, 1995 and the 1994 Rules.

The Inter-Departmental Committee (under the 2021 Amendment Rules) had flagged non-compliance; the advisory also asks channels to use authentic maps of India and to sensitise editorial teams via workshops.

capsules.subject: Election Law
capsules.title: SC: no adjudication on EC's revised Form 6 (12 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: 12 Oct 2026: The Supreme Court (CJI Surya Kant, Justices Joymalya Bagchi & V. Mohana) clarified it had neither approved nor disapproved the EC's modified Form 6 declaration — the revised form (requiring SIR-linkage disclosures) did not exist when the May 27 Bihar SIR judgment was delivered; “there is no adjudication on the new Form 6.”

capsules.subject: Legal GK
capsules.title: CLAT 2027: notification out 15 Oct; register by 31 Oct
capsules.body: The Consortium of National Law Universities released the CLAT 2027 notification on 15 October 2026, opening registrations for BA LLB (Hons) and LLM programmes at 24 NLUs. Registration closes 31 October 2026 at consortiumofnlus.ac.in; the exam is on 6 December 2026 (2:00–4:00 PM). UG eligibility: Class 12 with 45% (40% SC/ST); marking +1/−0.25. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Legal GK
capsules.title: AILET 2027: apply by 10 Nov; exam 13 Dec 2026
capsules.body: AILET 2027, conducted by National Law University Delhi for admission to NLU Delhi only, has an application deadline of 10 November 2026 and the exam on 13 December 2026. Pattern: 150 questions across three sections, with 70 questions on Logical Reasoning. (Dated: 22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Current affairs
capsules.title: CLAT 2027: registration closes 31 Oct 2026; exam 6 Dec, 2–4 PM (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Consortium of NLUs will close CLAT 2027 applications at 11:59 PM on 31 October 2026 (registration open since 3 August; notification 22 July 2026). The exam is on Sunday, 6 December 2026, 2–4 PM, offline pen-and-paper, for UG and PG law programmes at 26 member NLUs. UG: 120 questions, 2 hours, +1/−0.25 marking; eligibility 45% in Class 12 (40% SC/ST); PG: 50% in LLB (45% SC/ST); fee ₹4,000 (₹3,500 SC/ST/BPL/PwD); no upper age limit. Pattern unchanged this cycle; Expert Committee reforms apply from CLAT 2028. (22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Current affairs
capsules.title: AP High Court: 119 Civil Judge (Jr Division) posts; apply by 26 Oct 2026 (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The High Court of Andhra Pradesh at Amaravati invites applications for Civil Judge (Junior Division) in the AP State Judicial Service — 96 vacancies under Direct Recruitment and 23 under Recruitment by Transfer. Direct recruitment: law graduates who obtained their degree in the preceding one year as on the notification date. Last date for online application: 26.10.2026. (22 Oct 2026)

capsules.subject: Current affairs
capsules.title: MEA seeks Consultant (Legal) for Eurasia Division — 1 post; apply by 26 Oct 2026 (22 Oct 2026)
capsules.body: The Ministry of External Affairs (Administration Division, Advt No. Q/PF/575/50/2026 dated 5 Oct 2026) seeks 01 Consultant (Legal) for the Eurasia Division on a one-year contract (extendable; max ₹10,00,000/year). Essentials: bachelor's degree in law, 5+ years legal experience, 5 years in court-case processes, knowledge of international law and diplomatic norms; age ≤45 (≤63 for retired GoI servants). Apply by email/post on or before 26 October 2026 (17:30). (22 Oct 2026)

oneliners.text: Actus reus non facit reum nisi mens sit rea — an act alone does not make a person guilty unless the mind is guilty too.
Audi alteram partem — the rule that both sides must be heard before any decision is made against a person.
Nemo judex in causa sua — no one should be a judge in their own cause; the rule against bias.
Ignorantia juris non excusat — no one can escape legal liability by claiming they did not know the law.
Nulla poena sine lege — no punishment without a pre-existing law.
Actio personalis moritur cum persona — a personal cause of action dies with the person.
Caveat emptor — let the buyer beware; the buyer must examine goods before purchase.
Res ipsa loquitur — the thing speaks for itself; negligence may be inferred from the facts.
Volenti non fit injuria — to one who willingly accepts a risk, no legal injury is done.
Ex turpi causa non oritur actio — no legal action arises from an immoral or illegal cause.
Ubi jus ibi remedium — where there is a legal right, there is a legal remedy.
Damnum sine injuria — loss suffered without violation of a legal right gives no cause of action.
Injuria sine damnum — violation of a legal right is actionable even without actual loss.
Pacta sunt servanda — agreements must be kept; the foundation of treaty law.
Res judicata — a matter already decided by a competent court cannot be re-litigated between the same parties.
Stare decisis — courts stand by decided cases; the doctrine of binding precedent.
Ratio decidendi — the legal reason behind a decision; the binding part of a judgment.
Obiter dicta — a judge’s passing remarks; persuasive but not binding on later courts.
Per incuriam — a decision given in ignorance of a statute or binding precedent; it carries no authority.
De minimis non curat lex — the law does not concern itself with trifles.
Fiat justitia ruat caelum — let justice be done though the heavens fall.
Salus populi suprema lex esto — the welfare of the people is the supreme law.
Necessitas non habet legem — necessity knows no law.
Qui facit per alium facit per se — one who acts through another acts himself; the basis of agency law.
Delegatus non potest delegare — a delegate cannot further delegate the authority entrusted to them.
Nemo dat quod non habet — no one can transfer a better title than they themselves possess.
In pari delicto potior est conditio defendentis — where both parties are equally at fault, the defendant’s position is stronger.
Ex nudo pacto non oritur actio — no action arises from a bare promise without consideration.
Consensus ad idem — agreement upon the same thing in the same sense; essential for a valid contract.
Vigilantibus non dormientibus jura subveniunt — the law aids the vigilant, not those who sleep on their rights.
Cessante ratione legis cessat ipsa lex — when the reason for a law ceases, the law itself ceases.
Expressio unius est exclusio alterius — the express mention of one thing implies the exclusion of others.
Ejusdem generis — general words following specific ones are read as being of the same kind.
Noscitur a sociis — a word is known by the company it keeps.
Reddendo singula singulis — each word or phrase is referred to its matching counterpart.
Generalia specialibus non derogant — general provisions do not override special ones.
Lex specialis derogat legi generali — a special law prevails over a general law.
Lex posterior derogat priori — a later law repeals an earlier inconsistent law.
Jus in rem is a right against the world at large; jus in personam is a right against a specific person.
Ultra vires means beyond legal power; intra vires means within legal power.
Ab initio means from the beginning; an act void ab initio was never valid in law.
Sine die means without fixing a day; an adjournment sine die is indefinite.
Doli incapax means incapable of crime; a child below seven years is conclusively doli incapax.
Res gestae are facts forming part of the same transaction; they are admissible under Section 6 of the Indian Evidence Act.
Jus cogens is a peremptory norm of international law from which no derogation is permitted.
Article 1 declares that India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States.
Article 3 empowers Parliament to form new states and alter the boundaries of existing states.
Article 12 defines ‘the State’ for the purposes of Part III fundamental rights.
Article 13 voids laws inconsistent with fundamental rights.
Article 14 guarantees equality before the law and equal protection of the laws.
Article 15 prohibits discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth.
Article 15(3) permits special provisions for women and children.
Article 15(4) permits special provisions for socially and educationally backward classes; it was added by the First Amendment in 1951.
Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in public employment.
Article 16(4) permits reservation in appointments for backward classes inadequately represented in state services.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice in any form.
Article 18 abolishes titles, except military and academic distinctions.
Article 19(1)(a) guarantees freedom of speech and expression, the source of press freedom.
Article 19(1)(g) guarantees the freedom to practise any profession or carry on any occupation, trade or business.
Article 20 protects against ex post facto laws, double jeopardy and self-incrimination.
Article 21 protects life and personal liberty; no person shall be deprived of it except by procedure established by law.
Article 21A makes free and compulsory education for children aged six to fourteen a fundamental right; added by the 86th Amendment in 2002.
Article 22 lays down safeguards against arrest and preventive detention, including the right to consult a lawyer.
Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour.
Article 24 prohibits employment of children below fourteen in factories, mines and hazardous work.
Article 25 guarantees freedom of conscience and the free profession, practice and propagation of religion.
Article 29 protects the language, script and culture of minorities.
Article 30 gives minorities the right to establish and administer educational institutions.
Article 32 gives the right to constitutional remedies; Ambedkar called it the ‘heart and soul’ of the Constitution.
Article 39A directs the State to provide free legal aid; it was inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976.
Article 40 directs the State to organise village panchayats.
Article 44 directs the State to endeavour to secure a uniform civil code for all citizens.
Article 48A directs the State to protect and improve the environment; inserted by the 42nd Amendment.
Article 50 directs the separation of the judiciary from the executive.
Article 51A lists eleven fundamental duties; the eleventh, on parents and guardians, was added by the 86th Amendment in 2002.
Article 61 lays down the procedure for impeachment of the President.
Article 72 gives the President the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites and remissions.
Article 74 provides for a Council of Ministers with the Prime Minister at the head to aid and advise the President.
Article 76 provides for the Attorney-General for India, the government’s chief legal adviser.
Article 108 provides for a joint sitting of both Houses of Parliament to break a deadlock on a bill.
Article 110 defines a Money Bill; the Speaker’s decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.
Article 112 provides for the Annual Financial Statement, popularly called the Union Budget.
Article 123 gives the President power to promulgate ordinances when Parliament is not in session.
Article 129 declares the Supreme Court a court of record with power to punish for contempt.
Article 136 gives the Supreme Court discretionary power to grant special leave to appeal from any court or tribunal.
Article 141 makes law declared by the Supreme Court binding on all courts in India.
Article 142 empowers the Supreme Court to pass any order necessary to do complete justice.
Article 143 lets the President seek the Supreme Court’s advisory opinion on questions of law or public importance.
Article 148 provides for the Comptroller and Auditor-General of India.
Article 161 gives the Governor pardoning powers similar to the President’s within the state sphere.
Article 200 gives the Governor four options on a bill: assent, withhold assent, return it once, or reserve it for the President.
Article 213 gives the Governor ordinance-making power when the state legislature is not in session.
Article 226 gives High Courts writ jurisdiction wider than the Supreme Court’s, since it covers legal rights as well as fundamental rights.
Article 227 gives High Courts superintendence over all subordinate courts and tribunals in the state.
Article 248 vests residuary legislative powers in Parliament.
Article 263 provides for the Inter-State Council, chaired by the Prime Minister.
Article 280 provides for the Finance Commission, constituted every five years.

Article 300A makes the right to property a constitutional right: no person shall be deprived of property except by authority of law; it was moved out of fundamental rights by the 44th Amendment in 1978.
Article 312 lets Parliament create All-India Services on a Rajya Sabha resolution.
Article 324 vests superintendence, direction and control of elections in the Election Commission.
Article 326 provides for elections on the basis of adult suffrage.
Article 343 adopts Hindi in Devanagari script as the official language of the Union.
Article 352 provides for a National Emergency on grounds of war, external aggression or armed rebellion.
Article 356 provides for President’s Rule in a state on failure of constitutional machinery.
Article 360 provides for a Financial Emergency; it has never been proclaimed.
Article 368 lays down the procedure for amending the Constitution.
Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (1973) — propounded the basic structure doctrine: Parliament cannot destroy the Constitution’s essential features.
Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967) — held fundamental rights could not be amended; overruled by Kesavananda Bharati.
Minerva Mills v. Union of India (1980) — struck down parts of the 42nd Amendment; harmony between fundamental rights and directive principles is part of the basic structure.
Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India (1978) — Article 21 procedure must be fair, just and reasonable, not merely any enacted procedure.
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras (1950) — gave Article 21 its early narrow ‘procedure established by law’ reading.
ADM Jabalpur v. Shivkant Shukla (1976) — the habeas corpus case; the majority upheld suspension of Article 21 during the Emergency; overruled by Puttaswamy in 2017.
K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017) — a nine-judge bench recognised the right to privacy as part of Article 21.
Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India (2018) — upheld Aadhaar 4:1 with safeguards, striking down mandatory bank and mobile linking.
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) — curbed misuse of Article 356; secularism is part of the basic structure.
I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007) — Ninth Schedule laws inserted after 24 April 1973 are open to basic-structure review.
Waman Rao v. Union of India (1981) — Ninth Schedule amendments made after Kesavananda’s date must satisfy the basic structure test.
Shankari Prasad v. Union of India (1951) — upheld the First Amendment, holding Parliament could amend fundamental rights.
Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan (1965) — upheld the Seventeenth Amendment on land reform.
State of Madras v. Champakam Dorairajan (1951) — fundamental rights prevail over directive principles; the ruling led to the First Amendment.
E.P. Royappa v. State of Tamil Nadu (1973) — arbitrariness is the antithesis of Article 14 equality.
State of West Bengal v. Anwar Ali Sarkar (1952) — laid down Article 14’s twin test: intelligible differentia with a rational nexus to the legislative object.
M.R. Balaji v. State of Mysore (1963) — caste cannot be the sole test of backwardness; reservation should generally stay below fifty percent.
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (1992) — the Mandal case; upheld 27% OBC reservation, capped total reservation at 50% and excluded the creamy layer.
Ashoka Kumar Thakur v. Union of India (2008) — upheld 27% OBC quota in central educational institutions with creamy-layer exclusion.
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India (2006) — laid down conditions of backwardness, inadequate representation and efficiency for SC/ST reservation in promotions.
Jarnail Singh v. Lachhmi Narain Gupta (2018) — creamy-layer exclusion applies to SC/ST reservation in promotions too.
State of Punjab v. Davinder Singh (2024) — a seven-judge bench allowed states to sub-classify Scheduled Castes for reservation purposes.
Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India (2022) — upheld the 103rd Amendment creating 10% EWS reservation.
T.M.A. Pai Foundation v. State of Karnataka (2002) — defined the rights of minority educational institutions under Article 30.
Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh (1993) — read the right to education into Article 21, paving the way for the 86th Amendment.
Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka (1992) — struck down capitation fees charged by professional colleges.
Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) — laid down workplace sexual-harassment guidelines; the basis of the 2013 POSH Act.
Olga Tellis v. Bombay Municipal Corporation (1985) — the right to livelihood is part of Article 21’s right to life.
Hussainara Khatoon v. State of Bihar (1979) — read speedy trial and free legal aid into Article 21.
D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal (1996) — laid down guidelines on arrest and custodial interrogation.
Nilabati Behera v. State of Orissa (1993) — awarded compensation for custodial death under Article 21.
Rudul Sah v. State of Bihar (1983) — the first case awarding compensation for illegal detention under Article 32.
Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab (1980) — the death penalty is valid only in the ‘rarest of rare’ cases.
Machhi Singh v. State of Punjab (1983) — elaborated the rarest-of-rare guidelines for awarding the death penalty.
Mithu v. State of Punjab (1983) — struck down the mandatory death penalty in Section 303 of the IPC.
Shatrughan Chauhan v. Union of India (2014) — inordinate delay in deciding mercy petitions is a ground for commuting a death sentence.
Lalita Kumari v. State of Uttar Pradesh (2013) — registration of an FIR is mandatory on disclosure of a cognizable offence.
Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar (2014) — police must follow Section 41 CrPC safeguards before arrest in offences punishable up to seven years.
Joginder Kumar v. State of Uttar Pradesh (1994) — arrest is not routine; reasons must be recorded.
State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (1992) — laid down guidelines for quashing an FIR under Section 482 CrPC.
Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia v. State of Punjab (1980) — the leading case on anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC.
